Rounds a number to the specified precision, pads trailing decimal zeros, optionally applies thousands separators unless suppressed, returns "0" for zero, and returns a formatted numeric string.
Rounds a number to the given precision, returns "0" if num is 0, pads decimals, optionally adds thousands separators unless suppressed, and returns integer-only when precision is 0.

Rounds num to the given precision, pads missing fractional zeros, optionally adds thousands separators unless suppressed, and returns "0" for zero, integer part for precision 0, otherwise decimal string.
Rounds a number to the specified decimal precision, returning "0" for zero input, returning only the integer part when precision is zero, and optionally applying thousands separators.
Creates a new object by iterating default keys, assigning source values when the source contains the key, otherwise assigning default values, and returns the merged result.
`merge_or_apply` builds and returns a new object by reducing `defaults` keys, using `source[key]` when `key` exists in `sourceKeys` (`indexOf(key) > -1`), otherwise `defaults[key]`.
It returns an object built by reducing default keys, assigning each key from source when sourceKeys contains it (indexOf > -1), otherwise from defaults.
Returns an object built from defaults’ keys, using source values when source contains the same key, otherwise falling back to the corresponding defaults values.
Calculates a suggested tick count for a two-value domain by finding the smallest scaled base interval meeting range/10 and dividing evenly into the range, otherwise returning 11.
Calculates a suggested tick count for a two-value domain by filtering scaled base intervals ≥ range/10, returning range/interval+1 for the first exact divisor, otherwise 11.
Calculates a suggested tick count for a two-value domain by finding scaled intervals meeting a minimum, returning range/interval+1 when range is divisible, otherwise 11.
Calculates a suggested tick count from a domain by deriving interval candidates from range magnitude, returning (range/interval)+1 when range divides a candidate exactly, otherwise 11.

Determines locale-specific decimal and thousands separators from 1000.50 by comparing `toLocaleString()` and `toString()` characters, defaulting to "." and "," when they match, and returns both separators.
detectNumberSeparators derives locale decimal and thousands separators from 1000.50’s localized string, defaulting to “.” or “,” when localized substrings match the plain string, and returns both.

detectNumberSeparators derives decimal and thousands separators from 1000.50’s locale string, defaulting to "." and "," when locale substrings match plain toString output, and returns them in an object.
detectNumberSeparators compares locale-formatted and plain string forms of 1000.50 by checking characters at positions 1 and 5, then returns an object containing detected separators.
Creates a transformer that, when given an AST and file with a path, gathers references, adds unique same-hash cross-file pathnames to fileSet, records landmarks, and stores both on file.data.

Creates and returns a transformer that skips files without `file.path`, gathers references, adds unique hashed external pathnames to `fileSet`, marks file/heading landmarks, and stores references/landmarks in `file.data`.

Creates and returns a transformer that, when file.path exists, gathers references, adds unique hashed external pathnames to fileSet, marks file/heading landmarks, and stores references/landmarks on file.data.
Creates and returns a transformer using the provided fileSet and info inputs, with no explicit conditions, asynchronous behavior, function calls, or error handling.

Validates each file reference by checking exposed targets or filesystem existence, then warns for unknown files/headings (including cross-file headings), optionally suggesting the closest known reference.
Validates each file reference by checking exposed targets, optional filesystem existence for non-hash links, and heading hashes, then warns unknown links with optional closest-match suggestions.
Validates file references by checking exposed mappings, hash/path existence, and filesystem fallback, then warns unknown files/headings (with closest suggestion) via warnAll and returns nothing.
Iterates over references, computes each hash, checks whether the decoded reference exists under file.cwd, derives pathname and closest exposed match, and issues warnings via warnAll.

Processes a resource node URL (or identifier definition), normalizes/remaps local or allowed prefixed-domain links, ignores missing/invalid ones, and caches the node by pathname and optional non-line hash.

Processes a resource node URL (or identifier definition), normalizes/resolves local or same-domain links under required prefix, strips line hashes when configured, caches nodes by pathname/hash, and otherwise returns early.

Processes a node URL (or identifier definition), normalizes/resolves local or same-domain links with prefix checks, filters invalid/external cases, and caches the node under pathname and optional hash link.

Processes a node resource link by validating parsed URL/domain/path prefix and file context, normalizing or splitting line/heading/hash targets, caching the node by path/link, and otherwise returning undefined.
Iterates over each node in `nodes`, issuing `file.message(reason, node, sourceId + ':' + ruleId)` for each, and returns `undefined`.
`warnAll` iterates over `nodes`, and for each node calls `file.message(reason, node, [sourceId, ruleId].join(':'))`, returning `undefined` after processing all nodes.
`warnAll(file, nodes, reason, ruleId)` iterates over `nodes`, calling `file.message(reason, node, [sourceId, ruleId].join(':'))` for each node, and returns nothing.
warnAll iterates through nodes with forEach, processing each node via one using file, reason, and ruleId, and does not explicitly return a value.
Computes the closest match for a pathname by collecting matching reference hashes when bases match and both have hashes, or bases when neither has hashes, then returns propose’s result.
Builds candidate matches from references sharing pathname/hash conditions with the input pathname, then returns propose(hash or base, dictionary, {threshold: 0.7}).

Computes pathname hash/base, collects matching reference subhashes when bases match and both hashes exist, or subbases when neither hash exists, then returns propose(hash||base, dictionary, {threshold:0.7}).
Builds arrays of each reference’s hash and pathname, then returns propose(hash if present else base pathname, those arrays, with a 0.7 threshold).
Parses the URI, checks whether a hash fragment exists, and returns the fragment without the leading “#”, or null if no hash is present.
getHash parses the given URI, reads its hash property, and returns the hash without its first character when present, otherwise returns null.
`getHash` parses `uri`, reads its `hash` property, and returns `hash.slice(1)` when `hash` is truthy; otherwise it returns `null`.
Parses the URI and returns the hash fragment without the leading “#” when a hash exists; otherwise, it returns null.
Returns the contents of a previous source map file when `options.map.prev` is a string and the constructed map path exists; otherwise it returns nothing.

Returns the contents of a previous source map file if `typeof options.map.prev === 'string'` and `grunt.file.exists(mapPath)` for `options.map.prev + path.basename(from) + '.map'`; otherwise returns nothing.
Returns `grunt.file.read(mapPath)` when `options.map.prev` is a string, building `mapPath` as `options.map.prev + path.basename(from) + '.map'` and requiring `grunt.file.exists(mapPath)`.
Returns the previous map file contents if `options.map.prev` is truthy and the derived `mapPath` exists; otherwise returns nothing.
Parses a dotted IPv4 string into a 32-bit integer, throwing TypeError if input is not a string or does not contain exactly four dot-separated octets.
Parses a string IPv4 address into four base-10 octets, throws TypeError if input isn’t a string or doesn’t contain exactly four octets, and returns its uint32 numeric value.
Parses a string IPv4 address, throwing TypeError if input isn’t a string or doesn’t contain exactly four dot-separated octets, and returns its computed 32-bit integer value.
Parses a string IPv4 address into a uint32, throwing TypeError if addr is not a string or if splitting by dots does not produce exactly four octets.
Retrieves `obj[prop]`, throwing an error if it is `undefined` while `Bottle.config.strict` is true, and otherwise returns the retrieved value.
`getNested(obj, prop)` retrieves `obj[prop]`, throws an Error if it is `undefined` while `Bottle.config.strict` is true, and otherwise returns the retrieved value.
`getNested(obj, prop)` retrieves `obj[prop]`, throws an Error when it is `undefined` and `Bottle.config.strict` is truthy, and otherwise returns the retrieved value.
Returns obj[prop], but if Bottle.config.strict is true and obj[prop] is undefined, it throws an Error indicating the requested service property is undefined.
Returns an existing nested bottle by name, or if absent creates one via `Bottle.pop()`, stores it, registers a factory returning its container, and returns it.
`getNestedBottle(name)` checks whether `this.nested[name]` exists; if not, it pops a `Bottle`, stores and factories it, then returns `this.nested[name]`.
`getNestedBottle(name)` checks whether `this.nested[name]` exists; if not, it pops a `Bottle`, stores it, registers a factory returning `bottle.container`, and returns `this.nested[name]`.
Removes a bottle from `Bottle.pop()`, registers a sub-provider factory for `name` returning that bottle’s container, and returns `this.nested[name]`.
Defines `container[name]` as either a getter that runs middleware sequentially on `instance` and throws on middleware errors, or a writable value, then returns `container[name]`.

Defines `container[name]` via a descriptor: if `middleware.length` is truthy, a getter runs middleware sequentially on `instance` and returns it; otherwise stores writable `instance`, then returns `container[name]`.

Defines `container[name]` via a descriptor: if `middleware.length` exists, sets a getter that runs middleware sequentially and returns `instance`; otherwise sets writable value `instance`, then returns `container[name]`.
Defines an enumerable, configurable property named `name` on `container` using `middleware`, `instance`, and `container`, then returns `container[name]`.

This function normalizes arguments when fullname is a function, splits fullname by a delimiter, recursively delegates nested middleware registration, stores func in this.middlewares[name], and returns this.

Registers a middleware function by fullname, treating a function fullname as global, splitting names by delimiter, nesting when parts remain, otherwise initializing/pushing into this.middlewares[name], and returning this.

Registers middleware by name or function: if fullname is a function, uses GLOBAL_NAME; splits fullname, delegates nested names, otherwise initializes/pushes into this.middlewares[name], and returns this.

Registers middleware by splitting `fullname`; if dynamic operation `typeof fullname` applies it delegates via nested bottle middleware, otherwise pushes `func` to `this.middlewares[name]`, returning `this`.

Defines lazy-loaded provider and service getters on `container`; service getter checks for an existing provider, applies global/name decorators and middleware, cleans cached entries, and returns `this`.

createProvider defines lazy container properties for name and name+PROVIDER_SUFFIX, instantiates Provider on first provider access, and when provider exists builds/decorates service then applies middleware unless undefined, returning this.
Creates lazy container properties for a provider and service name, instantiating Provider on first access, resolving/decorating/middleware-processing service if provider exists, and returning this.
Creates a null-prototype properties object, defines those properties on container, and returns this without checking any conditions.
Registers a provider by fullname, errors if a single-part provider is already instantiated, stores provider metadata, delegates nested names recursively, and returns this or createProvider’s result.

Registers a provider by fullname, errors and returns console.error if already mapped with single-part name and no container instance, otherwise stores mappings and returns this or createProvider.call(this,name,Provider).

Registers a provider by fullname, errors if already instantiated with no nesting, stores mappings, delegates nested names to getNestedBottle(...).provider(...) returning this, otherwise returns createProvider.call(this,name,Provider).
Registers a provider by fullname, returning this for nested names, logging an error if a top-level provider is already instantiated, otherwise creating and returning the provider.
Defines an own property on this object with the given name and value, returning undefined, and sets it as configurable, enumerable, and writable.
Defines a property named `name` on `this` via `Object.defineProperty` with `val` as its value, setting `configurable`, `enumerable`, and `writable` to `true`, and returns nothing.
defineValue defines a property named by name on this via Object.defineProperty with configurable, enumerable, and writable all true, value set to val, and returns undefined.
Defines an enumerable, configurable, writable property named `name` on `this` with value `val` using `Object.defineProperty`, and returns nothing.
Returns `container[name]` if it exists; otherwise creates an empty object, assigns it to `container[name]` via `defineValue`, and returns the newly assigned object.
setValueObject gets container[name], and if it is falsy creates an empty object, assigns it via defineValue.call(container, name, nestedContainer), then returns nestedContainer.
`setValueObject` gets `container[name]`, creates an empty object and assigns it via `defineValue.call(container, name, nestedContainer)` if missing, then returns `nestedContainer`.
Creates and assigns a nestedContainer value on container under name using defineValue.call, then returns the nestedContainer.
Splits a delimited property path, traverses/creates nested objects in `this.container`, defines `val` on the final property name, and returns the current object (`this`).
Splits `name` by `DELIMITER`, pops the final segment as the property name, defines `val` on the nested object built from remaining segments in `this.container`, and returns `this`.
Splits name by DELIMITER, pops the last segment as name, defines val via defineValue.call on the reduced container path, and returns this.
Sets a nested value in this.container by splitting the path, reducing parent objects with setValueObject, defining the final key with val, and returning this.
Splits a delimited constant name, resolves or creates nested container objects from preceding parts, defines the constant on the final segment, and returns the current object (`this`).
Splits a delimited constant name into parts, pops the final name segment, defines the constant on the reduced container path with the given value, and returns this.
Splits `name` by `DELIMITER`, pops the final segment as the constant name, defines it via `defineConstant.call` on a reduced container path, and returns `this`.
Defines a constant named by the last segment of a delimiter-split path on this.container via defineConstant, assigning the given value, and returns this.
Registers a decorator function by parsing a dotted fullname, defaulting fullname when given a function, recursing for nested names, storing functions in this.decorators, and returning this.
Registers a decorator function under a dotted fullname, treating fullname as func when it’s a function, nesting via getNestedBottle when parts remain, and returning this.

Registers a decorator function by fullname: if fullname is a function, uses GLOBAL_NAME; splits name, nests via getNestedBottle when parts remain, otherwise initializes/pushes this.decorators[name], then returns this.
Adds a decorator function by splitting fullname, delegating nested names to getNestedBottle(...).decorator(...), otherwise pushing func into this.decorators[name], and returns this.
Creates and returns a factory via `factory.call(this, name, ...)` that provides an object whose `instance` property is `Factory` bound to `Factory` and the given `container`.
`instanceFactory` calls `factory.call(this, name, GenericInstanceFactory)` and returns its result, where `GenericInstanceFactory(container)` returns `{ instance: Factory.bind(Factory, container) }`.
Creates an instance factory by calling `factory.call(this, name, GenericInstanceFactory)`, where `GenericInstanceFactory(container)` returns `{ instance: Factory.bind(Factory, container) }`.
Calls `factory` with `this`, `name`, and a `GenericInstanceFactory` callback that returns an object whose `instance` is `Factory` bound to `Factory` and `container`, returning that result.
Returns an existing Bottle by string name from `bottles`, creating and storing one with `BOTTLE_NAME` set if missing; for non-string input, returns a new Bottle.
Returns a Bottle by name: if name is a string, it gets bottles[name], creates/stores a new Bottle and sets BOTTLE_NAME when missing, otherwise returns a new Bottle.
Returns bottles[name] when name is a string, creating and storing a new Bottle with constant('BOTTLE_NAME', name) if missing; otherwise returns a new Bottle instance.
Returns the Bottle instance immediately if name is a string; otherwise creates a Bottle, sets constant BOTTLE_NAME to name, and returns a new Bottle instance.
Registers an object by selecting its value from `$value` or itself, then invokes the specified `$type` method (default `service`) with `$name`, value, and optional `$inject` arguments.
Registers an object by choosing Obj.$value unless undefined (then Obj), selecting this[Obj.$type||'service'], and returning its apply(this, [Obj.$name, value].concat(Obj.$inject||[])) result.
`register(Obj)` sets `value` to `Obj` when `Obj.$value===undefined` otherwise `Obj.$value`, then returns `this[Obj.$type||'service'].apply(this, [Obj.$name, value].concat(Obj.$inject||[]))`.
Registers an object by invoking this[Obj.$type or 'service'] with Obj.$name, Obj.$value if defined otherwise Obj, plus any Obj.$inject entries, and returns that invocation’s result.

Resets providers from originalProviders, optionally only for names in an array, removing nested mappings when names contain the delimiter, then re-registering each selected provider from the original map.

Resets providers from `this.originalProviders`, optionally filtering by `names` when it is an array, removes mapped providers (including nested-delimited parts), and re-registers each selected original provider.

Resets this.originalProviders entries, optionally filtering by names array membership, removes provider maps (including nested parts split by DELIMITER), re-registers each provider, and returns nothing.
Resets providers from `this.originalProviders`, optionally filtering by an array of names, removing mapped nested and direct providers, then restoring each selected provider from `tempProviders`.
Validates that `node` is an AST node using `exports.isASTNode`; if not, it throws an `Error` including `functionName` and an inspected representation of `node`.
Validates that `node` is an AST node using `exports.isASTNode`; if not, throws `Error(functionName + "(): " + util.inspect(node) + " is not a valid AST node.")`, otherwise returns nothing.
`throwIfInvalidNode(node, functionName)` checks whether `exports.isASTNode(node)` is false and, if so, throws an `Error` including `functionName` and `util.inspect(node)`; otherwise returns nothing.
Throws an Error naming the function and inspected value when `node` is not a valid AST node (`!exports.isASTNode(node)`); otherwise it returns nothing.
Checks whether an expression calls a declared event by matching callee and event names and verifying contract enclosure, returning true on match and false otherwise.
Checks each event declaration and returns true if expr.callee.name equals a declaration’s node.name and expr is a child of its enclosingContract; otherwise returns false.
Checks whether expr matches any event declaration by callee name and being a child of that declaration’s enclosingContract, returning true on first match, otherwise false.
Checks whether an expression calls any declared event within its enclosing contract by matching callee and event names and child relationship, returning true if matched, otherwise false.
Adds an event’s node and its enclosing contract to `events` when `emitted.exit` is falsy, and otherwise does nothing.
`registerEventName` extracts `node` from `emitted`, and if `emitted.exit` is falsy, pushes `{ node, enclosingContract: sourceCode.getParent(node) }` into `events`, returning nothing.

registerEventName destructures node from emitted and, if emitted.exit is falsy, pushes {node, enclosingContract: sourceCode.getParent(node)} into events, returning the push expression result otherwise falsey.
Registers an emitted event by pushing an object containing node and its enclosing contract from sourceCode.getParent(node) into the events array.
`inspectVariableDeclarator` stores `emitted.node` in `allVariableDeclarations` under `node.id.name` only when `emitted.exit` is falsy, and otherwise performs no action.
inspectVariableDeclarator gets emitted.node, and if emitted.exit is falsy, stores node in allVariableDeclarations keyed by node.id.name, otherwise returning without changes.
inspectVariableDeclarator gets emitted.node, and if emitted.exit is falsy, stores node in allVariableDeclarations keyed by node.id.name, returning undefined.
inspectVariableDeclarator takes emitted as input and has no specified conditions, calls, asynchronous behavior, errors, or return value.
If `emitted.exit` is truthy, reports each variable in `allVariableDeclarations` via `context.report` as declared but never used; otherwise it does nothing and returns undefined.
`inspectProgram(emitted)` checks whether `emitted.exit` is truthy, then reports each key in `allVariableDeclarations` via `context.report` as an unused variable, and returns nothing.
inspectProgram checks whether emitted.exit is truthy and, if so, reports each key in allVariableDeclarations as an unused variable via context.report; otherwise it returns nothing.
Iterates over all keys in `allVariableDeclarations` and reports each corresponding node to `context` with a message that the variable is declared but never used.
If not exiting, it gets the node and source code, and deletes allVariableDeclarations[node.name] when that declaration exists and the parent isn’t a VariableDeclarator.
If emitted.exit is falsy, it gets emitted.node and source code, then deletes allVariableDeclarations[node.name] when present and node’s parent type is not "VariableDeclarator".
inspectIdentifier checks emitted.exit, then if allVariableDeclarations[node.name] exists and node’s parent type isn’t "VariableDeclarator", deletes that entry, otherwise returns nothing.
Deletes the entry keyed by node.name from allVariableDeclarations after obtaining sourceCode from context and retrieving the parent of node via sourceCode.getParent(node).

If not exiting, it scans contract body function/constructor nodes, skipping ignored or correctly ordered visibility, updates order cursor when later-valid, and reports nodes violating expected function order.

inspectFunctionsOfContract exits if emitted.exit is set; otherwise it checks contract body function/constructor nodes for ignore/visibility/order conditions, reports misordered functions via context.report, and returns undefined.

Inspects contract body functions/constructors, skipping when emitted.exit, ignored by options, or visibility-matching expected order; updates cursor by order position and reports out-of-order functions via context.report.

Processes non-exit emissions by iterating contract function/constructor declarations, skipping ignored or correctly ordered/visible ones, updating cursor when order advances, and reporting misordered functions; returns undefined on exit.
Checks an experimental pragma statement’s position, skipping exited nodes, and reports/fixes it by moving it before the first non-pragma node unless only pragma statements precede it.
Checks an emitted pragma node’s position in program body, and if any preceding node isn’t ExperimentalPragmaStatement or PragmaStatement, reports and auto-fixes by moving the pragma before it.
Checks an emitted pragma node’s position, returning early if exited or reached itself, and reports/fixes when a preceding program body node isn’t ExperimentalPragmaStatement or PragmaStatement.
Checks an experimental pragma statement’s placement in program body, returning undefined on exit or matching start, otherwise reporting when disallowed nodes appear above and suggesting a move fix.

inspectTopLevelDeclaration skips processing when emitted.exit is true; otherwise it checks each top-level child’s start and end-line indentation against base rules, reporting violations and returning undefined.

Inspects emitted.node.body children for required base indentation, skipping when emitted.exit or single-line nodes, reporting misindented starts/ending lines (with extra indent for abstract functions), and returns undefined.
Inspects emitted.node.body declarations, skipping when emitted.exit is true, and reports indentation violations for child starts and ending lines (including abstract functions), returning nothing.
Inspects top-level declarations by iterating over body children after creating indentation-matching regexes, and returns undefined immediately when emitted.exit is truthy.

Checks multi-line block statements on entry, validates parent indentation matches base style, then reports each body item (and multi-line ending lines except IfStatement/chaining cases) not indented one level deeper.
inspectBlockStatement validates block-item indentation unless emitted.exit is set, the block is single-line, or parent indentation is nonstandard, reporting mismatches and returning undefined.

inspectBlockStatement validates block-item indentation unless exiting or single-line, ensuring parent indentation matches base style, reporting misindented starts/ends (with IfStatement exception), and otherwise returns nothing.

Processes a block statement only when not exiting, multiline, and parent indentation matches expected level, then computes next-level indent details and inspects each block item; otherwise returns undefined.
If not exiting, it scans a variable declaration’s text for “=” and reports when either side lacks exactly one adjacent space, otherwise returning nothing.
Inspects emitted.node variable-declaration text, exits if emitted.exit is truthy, then for each “=” reports when left or right adjacent spacing around it is not exactly one space.
Processes an emitted variable declaration, exits early if emitted.exit is truthy, scans for '=' characters, reports spacing violations on either side, and otherwise returns nothing.
If not exiting, it scans variable declaration text and reports when spacing around '=' is not exactly one space on either left or right side.

Creates a rule context object that conditionally adds options, defines read-only name/meta, proxies inheritable Solium methods, and reports validated errors augmented with ruleName, ruleMeta, and type.

Creates a rule context object, optionally copies ruleDesc.options, defines immutable name/meta, proxies inheritable Solium methods, validates report errors, enriches them, and returns via Solium.report.

Initializes a rule context by copying options if present, defining immutable name/meta, inheriting Solium methods, and adding report(error) that validates errors, enriches them, then calls Solium.report.
Initializes a rule context by setting options, defining immutable name and meta properties, and attaching methods that delegate to corresponding Solium methods with forwarded arguments.

Resolves an upstream ruleset by loading `solium:<name>` core rules (or throwing if missing), otherwise requiring a prefixed sharable config, validating it, and returning its `rules` or detailed errors.
Resolves an upstream ruleset by loading core `solium:*` configs or prefixed sharable configs, returning their `rules`, and throwing descriptive errors for missing, unloadable, or invalid configs.

Resolves an upstream ruleset by loading core `solium:*` or prefixed sharable configs, returning their `rules` when valid, otherwise throwing descriptive errors for missing, invalid, or unloadable modules.

Resolves an upstream ruleset by loading core `solium:*` configs or sharable configs, validating structure, and returning `rules`, while throwing specific errors for missing, invalid, or unresolvable configs.
Creates and returns an object mapping each `plugin.rules` key to `name/ruleName`, with values set to each rule’s `meta.docs.type`.
Builds and returns a config object mapping each `plugin.rules` key to `plugin.rules[ruleName].meta.docs.type`, using keys formatted as `name/ruleName`.
Creates and returns a config object mapping each `plugin.rules` key to its `meta.docs.type`, using keys formatted as `name/ruleName` for every rule.
Builds and returns a config object mapping each `plugin.rules` entry to its `meta.docs.type` under keys formatted as `name/ruleName`, iterating over all rule names.
Writes the config object as pretty-printed JSON to SOLIUMRC_FILENAME_ABSOLUTE, and on write errors reports a fatal message with the error text then exits with WRITE_FAILED.
Writes the given config as pretty-printed JSON to SOLIUMRC_FILENAME_ABSOLUTE, and if writing throws an error, reports a fatal message and exits with errorCodes.WRITE_FAILED, returning nothing.
Writes the config object as pretty-printed JSON to SOLIUMRC_FILENAME_ABSOLUTE, and if writing throws an error, reports a fatal message and exits with errorCodes.WRITE_FAILED.
Writes the config object as pretty JSON to SOLIUMRC_FILENAME_ABSOLUTE, and on write failure reports a fatal error with the exception message and exits with WRITE_FAILED.
Lints source code with optional autofix/dry-run, handling SyntaxError as a lint error and other exceptions as fatal, reports issues/diffs/fixes, and returns the count of errors.

Lints source code with optional autofix/dryrun, applies or reports diffs, handles syntax versus non-syntax exceptions differently, reports found issues, and returns the count of lint errors typed "error".

Lints source code with optional autofix/dry-run, handles non-syntax exceptions as fatal exits, converts syntax errors into lint errors, reports findings, and returns the count of errors typed "error".
`lintString` lints and auto-fixes source code, reports diffs and lint results, handles linting failures fatally, and returns the count of lint errors with type `"error"`.
Reads a file synchronously as UTF-8, reports a fatal error and exits with FILE_NOT_FOUND if reading fails, otherwise returns lintString(sourceCode, userConfig, errorReporter, fileName).
Reads a file as UTF-8, reports a fatal error and exits with FILE_NOT_FOUND if reading fails, then returns lintString(sourceCode, userConfig, errorReporter, fileName).
Reads a file’s UTF-8 contents, reports a fatal error and exits with FILE_NOT_FOUND if reading fails, otherwise returns lintString(sourceCode, userConfig, errorReporter, fileName).
Reads a file’s UTF-8 contents, reports a fatal error and exits with FILE_NOT_FOUND if reading fails, otherwise returns lintString(sourceCode, userConfig, errorReporter, fileName).
Configures the CLI object with version, description, usage, and linting options, using a collector to accumulate repeated --rule and --plugin values into arrays.
Configures and returns the passed CLI object with version/description/usage and many options, using a collect callback to accumulate repeated --rule and --plugin values into arrays.
createCliOptions configures cliObject with version, description, usage, and many options, using collect to accumulate repeated --rule and --plugin values into arrays, and returns the chained result.
Configures the CLI object with version, description, usage, and linting options (files, config, reporting, fixes, watch, ignore/rc toggles, rules, plugins), returning no value.
inspectFD returns early if exiting or no visibility modifier exists, otherwise reports an issue when any non-visibility modifier appears before the first visibility modifier in node.modifiers.
Checks a node’s modifiers and, unless exiting or no visibility modifier exists, reports when a non-visibility modifier precedes the first visibility modifier, otherwise returns nothing.
Checks emitted.node modifiers, exits if emitted.exit or no visibility modifier, and reports via context.report when any non-visibility modifier appears before the first visibility modifier.
Reports an issue via `context.report` unless `emitted.exit` is true or no visibility modifier exists, in which case it returns `undefined` after checking modifier ordering.
Checks whether a string starts with "0x" and has only hexadecimal digits afterward (case-insensitive), returning true if valid and false otherwise.
Checks whether a string starts with "0x" and has only hexadecimal digits afterward (case-insensitive), returning false if the prefix is missing, otherwise the regex test result.
Checks whether a string starts with "0x" and whether the remaining characters match one or more hexadecimal digits, returning false otherwise or the regex test result.
Checks whether a string starts with "0x" and has only hexadecimal characters afterward, returning false if the prefix is missing, otherwise the regex test result.

loadModule returns a cached modules[moduleName] if defined; otherwise it requires one of four named modules, throws on unknown names, caches the result, and returns it.
Returns an existing module if defined; otherwise, for charset, encoding, language, or mediaType it requires and returns the corresponding ./lib module, else throws a “Cannot find module” error.
Splits an Accept-Language header by commas, parses each trimmed entry with its index, keeps only truthy parsed languages, and returns the filtered array.
`parseAcceptLanguage` splits the `accept` string by commas, parses each trimmed entry with `parseLanguage`, keeps only truthy parsed languages, compacts the array, and returns it.
Parses a comma-separated Accept-Language string, trims and parseLanguage-processes each entry, keeps only truthy parsed languages, compacts the array length, and returns the filtered languages array.
Splits the input Accept-Language string by commas, trims and parses each entry with its index in a loop, and returns the resulting accepts array.
Parses a language tag string with an optional suffix and parameters, returns null if regex matching fails, otherwise returns prefix, suffix, combined full tag, q value, and index i.

Parses a language string with simpleLanguageRegExp, returns null if no match, otherwise builds prefix/suffix/full, extracts optional q from semicolon-separated parameters, and returns {prefix,suffix,q,i,full}.
Parses a language tag string via regex, returning null if unmatched; otherwise extracts prefix/suffix, optional q parameter from semicolon-separated key-values, and returns {prefix,suffix,q,i,full}.
Parses a language token from `str`; if no regex match returns null, otherwise processes semicolon parameters to parse `q` and returns prefix/suffix, q, index `i`, and full match.
Returns the highest-priority match for a language by iterating accepted entries, using specify(), and replacing priority when spec exists and has greater s, then q, then o values.
Computes the best language match priority by iterating accepted entries, updating when a spec exists and has higher s, then q, then o values, and returns that priority object.
Computes a language’s best priority by scanning accepted entries, updating when specify(...) returns a spec with lower s, q, or o values, and returns the priority object.
Iterates through accepted entries, calling specify(language, accepted[i], index) for each, and returns priority.
Parses a language string, returns null if parsing fails or spec.full is non-wildcard and mismatched, otherwise returns index/spec metadata with a score for full/prefix match conditions.
Parses language, returns null if parsing fails or spec.full isn’t '*', otherwise computes bitmask s from case-insensitive full/prefix matches and returns {i:index,o:spec.i,q:spec.q,s}.
Parses language, returns null if parsing fails or spec.full isn’t '*', otherwise sets bitflags by case-insensitive full/prefix matches and returns {i:index,o:spec.i,q:spec.q,s}.
Returns null if parsed language is falsy or spec.full is not '*'; otherwise computes match score s from lowercase full/prefix comparisons and returns {i:index,o:spec.i,q:spec.q,s}.

Parses the Accept-Language header (treating undefined as “*”), then returns quality-filtered, specificity-sorted accepted languages, either all parsed languages or matching entries from a provided list.

Parses the Accept-Language header (defaulting undefined to “*”), then returns quality-filtered, specificity-sorted accepted languages, or, if provided exists, matching provided languages ordered by computed priority.

Parses the Accept-Language header (defaulting undefined to "*"), then returns quality-filtered, specificity-sorted accepted languages or, if provided exists, matching provided languages by computed priority order.

Parses the Accept-Language header (defaulting undefined to “*”), and returns sorted quality-matched languages from accepts when no provided list exists, otherwise matching provided languages by priority.
Compares two spec objects for sorting by descending `q`, then descending `s`, then ascending `o`, then ascending `i`, returning the first nonzero difference or `0`.
compareSpecs orders two objects by returning the first nonzero difference among b.q−a.q, b.s−a.s, a.o−b.o, and a.i−b.i, or 0 if all are equal.
compareSpecs compares two specs by returning the first nonzero difference among b.q−a.q, b.s−a.s, a.o−b.o, and a.i−b.i, or 0 if all are equal.
Compares two specs by sorting descending on q and s, then ascending on o and i, returning the first nonzero numeric difference or 0 if equal.
Splits an Accept-Charset header by commas, parses each trimmed entry with its index, keeps only truthy parsed charsets, trims the array to kept items, and returns it.
Parses a comma-separated Accept-Charset string, trims and parseCharset-processes each entry with its index, keeps only truthy parsed charsets, truncates the array to kept items, and returns it.
Parses a comma-separated Accept-Charset string, trims and parseCharset-processes each entry, keeps only truthy parsed charsets, compacts the array length to kept items, and returns it.
Parses a comma-separated Accept-Charset string by trimming and parsing each entry with its index in a loop, then returns the resulting accepts array.
Parses a charset token from a string using a regex, returns null if no match, otherwise extracts optional q parameter (default 1) and returns charset, q, and i.
Parses a charset string with `simpleCharsetRegExp`; returns null if no match, otherwise extracts charset, optional `q` parameter from semicolon-separated params, and returns `{ charset, q, i }`.
Parses `str` with `simpleCharsetRegExp`; if no match returns `null`, otherwise extracts charset, optional `q` from semicolon-separated params, and returns `{ charset, q, i }`.
Parses a charset entry from `str`, returning null if regex matching fails; otherwise scans semicolon parameters until `q`, parses its float value, and returns `{charset, q, i}`.
Returns the highest-priority specification for a charset by scanning accepted entries, updating when a valid spec has greater specificity, quality, or order, and defaulting to {o:-1,q:0,s:0}.
Computes a charset’s best priority by scanning accepted entries, updating when a spec exists and has higher s, then q, then o values, and returns that priority object.
Computes a charset’s best match priority by scanning accepted entries, updating when spec exists and current priority is lower by s, q, or o comparison, then returns priority.
Iterates through accepted charsets, calling specify(charset, accepted[i], index) for each, and returns priority after the loop.
Matches a spec to a charset case-insensitively, returns null if charset differs and spec.charset isn’t '*', otherwise returns an object with index, spec order, quality, and match flag.
Checks whether `spec.charset` case-insensitively matches `charset` or equals `'*'`; returns null if neither, otherwise returns `{i:index, o:spec.i, q:spec.q, s}` with match flag `s`.
Returns null unless spec.charset is '*' or case-insensitively equals charset; when matched, returns {i:index, o:spec.i, q:spec.q, s} with s bitwise-ORed with 1 on equality.
Returns null unless spec.charset is '*'; otherwise lowercases spec.charset and charset, then returns { i: index, o: spec.i, q: spec.q, s: s }.
Parses the Accept-Charset header (treating undefined as “*”), then returns quality-filtered, sorted accepted charsets, either all parsed charsets or matching entries from a provided list.

Parses the Accept-Charset header (defaulting undefined to "*"), then returns quality-filtered, specificity-sorted charsets: all accepted full charsets if none provided, otherwise provided charsets by priority.
Parses the Accept-Charset header (defaulting undefined to “*”), then returns quality-filtered, sorted charset names from accepts or, if provided exists, matching provided charsets by priority.

Parses the Accept-Charset header (defaulting undefined to “*” and falsy to “”), then returns quality-filtered, specificity-sorted charsets from accepts or prioritized provided charsets when provided exists.
Parses an encoding token from a string using a regex, returns null if no match, otherwise extracts optional q parameter (default 1) and returns {encoding, q, i}.
parseEncoding regex-matches str; if no match returns null, otherwise extracts encoding, optionally parses ';'-separated parameters for q via parseFloat, and returns {encoding, q, i}.
Parses an encoding string with simpleEncodingRegExp, returns null if no match, otherwise extracts encoding and optional q parameter (default 1) and returns {encoding, q, i}.
Parses an encoding from `str` using `simpleEncodingRegExp`; returns `null` if no match, otherwise extracts optional `q` from semicolon parameters (stopping at `q`) and returns `{encoding, q, i}`.
Iterates through accepted entries, computes each entry’s specification for the encoding and index, keeps the highest-ranked spec by s, then q, then o, and returns it (default {o:-1,q:0,s:0}).
Computes an encoding’s best priority by scanning accepted entries, updating when a valid spec has higher s, then q, then o values, and returns the priority object.
Returns the best matching encoding priority object by scanning accepted entries, updating when specify(...) succeeds and current priority has lower s, q, or o values, then returning priority.
Returns the priority from iterating accepted encodings, calling specify(encoding, accepted[i], index) for each entry, and ultimately returning the computed priority value.
Parses the Accept-Encoding header, then returns quality-filtered, sorted encodings—either all accepted encodings when none are provided, or the provided encodings ranked by acceptance priority.

Parses the Accept-Encoding header, and returns quality-filtered, specificity-sorted encodings: all accepted full encodings when none are provided, otherwise provided encodings ranked by computed priority.

Parses the Accept-Encoding header, then if provided is missing returns acceptable encodings by quality/specificity, otherwise ranks provided encodings by priority and returns the filtered, sorted matches.

Parses the Accept-Encoding header, and if provided encodings are absent returns acceptable encodings by quality/specificity; otherwise ranks provided encodings by priority and returns the sorted acceptable ones.
Parses an Accept header into media type objects by splitting and trimming entries, keeping only truthy parseMediaType results, and returns the filtered array.
`parseAccept` splits an Accept header into media-type strings, parses each trimmed entry with its index, keeps only truthy parsed results, truncates the array, and returns it.
`parseAccept` splits an Accept header, parses and trims each media type, keeps only truthy parsed results, compacts the array length to valid entries, and returns it.
Parses an Accept header into media types by splitting the input, trimming and parsing each entry in a loop, and returns the resulting accepts array.
Parses a media type string with optional parameters, returning null if it doesn’t match; otherwise extracts type/subtype, lowercased params, quoted values unwrapped, and q (default 1).
Parses a media type string with a regex, returns null if it doesn’t match, otherwise extracts type/subtype, parses parameters (unquoting values), captures q as float, and returns metadata object.
Parses a media type string with regex, returns null if unmatched, otherwise extracts type/subtype, lowercased parameters (unquoting quoted values), q from parameter q, and returns them with i.
Parses a media type string into type, subtype, parameters, and quality, returning null if the regex fails and stopping parameter parsing when the lowercase key equals `q`.
Iterates through accepted media specs, computes each spec’s match for the given type and index, keeps the highest-ranked by s, q, then o, and returns it or defaults.
Computes the best media-type priority for a type across accepted entries by comparing spec.s, then spec.q, then spec.o, updating when higher, and returns the priority object.
Computes media type priority by scanning accepted entries, updating when specify(...) returns a spec with lower s, q, or o values, and returns the best priority object.
Computes and returns a media type’s priority by iterating through accepted entries, calling specify(type, accepted[i], index) for each, and ultimately returning priority.
Parses a media type, verifies spec type/subtype and optional params match exactly or wildcard, returns null on mismatch/parse failure, otherwise returns {i:index,o:spec.i,q:spec.q,s:score}.
Parses a media type, validates type/subtype and optional params against spec (allowing '*' wildcards, case-insensitive), and returns null or {i:index,o:spec.i,q:spec.q,s:matchFlags}.
Parses a media type, validates type/subtype and params against spec (allowing '*' wildcards, case-insensitive), sets match flags, and returns {i,o,q,s} or null on mismatch.
Parses a media type and, only if parsed, matching wildcard type/subtype and case-insensitive parameter checks pass, returns `{i:index,o:spec.i,q:spec.q,s}`; otherwise returns `null`.
Parses the Accept header (defaulting undefined to */*), then returns quality-filtered, spec-sorted accepted media types, either all accepted types or matching provided types by priority.

Parses the Accept header (defaulting undefined to */*), then returns quality-filtered, specificity-sorted acceptable media types, either from accepts directly or matched/prioritized from provided types.
Parses the Accept header (defaulting undefined to */*), then returns quality-filtered, specificity-sorted acceptable media types, either from parsed accepts or mapped provided types by priority.
Returns sorted acceptable media types from `accept` when `provided` is absent, otherwise returns `provided` types prioritized against parsed `accept`, filtering by quality and sorting by specificity.
Counts and returns the number of double-quote characters in a string by repeatedly finding `"` with `indexOf` until no more matches are found.
`quoteCount` counts occurrences of the double-quote character in `string` by repeatedly calling `indexOf` until it returns `-1`, then returns the total count.
Counts double-quote characters in the input string by repeatedly searching from the current index while indexOf does not return -1, and returns the total count.
Counts and returns the number of double-quote characters in the input string by repeatedly finding `"` with `indexOf` until no more matches are found.
Splits a string at the first '=' character, returning [key, value]; if '=' is absent, returns [str, undefined] with the entire string as the key.
Splits a string at the first '='; if none exists it sets key to the whole string, otherwise key/value are substrings before/after '=', and returns [key, val].
Splits a string at the first '='; if none exists, sets key to the whole string, otherwise sets key before '=' and val after it, returning [key, val].
Splits the input string at the first '=' by finding its index, extracting substrings before and after it, and returning them as a [key, val] array.
Splits an Accept header string by commas, then recombines segments when the current part has an odd quote count, trims extras, and returns the corrected media-type array.
Splits an Accept header by commas, then merges segments while quoteCount(accepts[j]) is odd, and returns the compacted accepts array truncated to j+1 elements.
Splits an Accept header by commas, then merges segments based on whether accumulated quote counts are even or odd, truncates to merged entries, and returns the resulting array.
Splits the input accept string by commas, iterates through resulting parts while checking quoteCount on the current segment, and returns the accepts array.
Splits a string on semicolons, then recombines segments when preceding quotes are unbalanced, trims each resulting parameter, and returns the finalized array of parameters.
Splits a semicolon-delimited string, merges segments when quoteCount of the current merged part is odd, trims each resulting parameter, and returns the trimmed parameters array.
Splits a string by semicolons, merges segments when the current merged part has an odd quote count, trims each resulting parameter, and returns the cleaned parameter array.
Splits a string by semicolons, merges segments while quoteCount indicates unmatched quotes during iteration, trims each resulting parameter, and returns the processed parameters array.
Loads `./webpack.config.js`, sets `devtool` to `'inline-source-map'`, configures a preLoader for `.js/.jsx` files in `lib` using `isparta`, and returns the modified config.
loadWebpackConfig requires './webpack.config.js', sets devtool to 'inline-source-map', assigns module.preLoaders to an isparta rule for .js/.jsx files in lib, and returns webpackConfig.
loadWebpackConfig requires './webpack.config.js', sets devtool to 'inline-source-map', sets module.preLoaders to an isparta loader for .js/.jsx files in resolved 'lib', and returns webpackConfig.
Loads and returns the webpack configuration from './webpack.config.js', and also calls path.resolve('lib') without using its result.
Assigns `value` into `obj` at the nested `keyPath`, creating missing intermediate keys as empty objects when absent, and returns nothing (undefined).
Assigns a value into a nested object path, creating missing intermediate keys as empty objects when a key is not in the current object, and sets the final key.
Assigns value into obj at the final keyPath key, creating missing intermediate keys as empty objects while iterating to keyPath.length-1, and returns nothing.
Assigns a value into an object along a key path by iterating through path segments up to the last key index, without explicit async calls, errors, or direct return value.
Returns a comma-separated string of parsed selected filters when selectedValues is non-empty and entries have allowed component types with non-empty array or range start/end values; otherwise null.
Returns a joined filter string by parsing selectedValues entries whose componentType is allowed and value has length/start/end, when selectedValues exists and has keys; otherwise returns null.

Returns a comma-joined string of parsed filters from selectedValues entries whose componentType is allowed and whose value has length/start/end, otherwise returns null when selectedValues is empty/falsy.
Returns a comma-joined filter string from selectedValues entries whose componentType is allowed and whose value has length, start, or end; otherwise returns null.

Horseman initializes an instance (or returns a new one if called without `new`), builds PhantomJS options from defined settings/overrides, initializes state fields, and returns `prepare(...)` in `ready`.

Initializes a Horseman instance by enforcing constructor usage, merging defaults/options, conditionally mapping defined option fields into PhantomJS parameters, and returns a new instance or the prepare() readiness result.

Initializes a Horseman instance, returning a new one if not called with `new`, merges/defaults options, conditionally maps defined settings into PhantomJS parameters, and returns `this.ready = prepare(this, instantiationOptions)`.

Horseman initializes a Horseman instance, recursively reinvokes itself if not called with `new`, merges default/cloned options, applies `phantomOptions` overrides, prepares Phantom parameters, and returns nothing.
Creates an image from input, waits for it to load, reads the first row’s pixel RGB values via canvas, normalizes each channel to 0–1, and resolves a Promise with them.
getColors creates an image from input, waits for onload, reads the first-row pixel RGBA values across image width, normalizes RGB to 0–1 arrays, and returns a Promise resolving them.
getColors creates an image from input, waits for onload, draws it to a canvas, reads first-row RGB values normalized by 255, and returns a Promise resolving to that array.
Creates an image from input, on load draws its first row to a canvas, extracts normalized RGB values per pixel across width, and returns a Promise resolving to that array.
Creates and returns an array of `steps` cubehelix RGB colors normalized to 0–1 by generating each color at `i/steps` with `opts` and dividing channels by 255.
createCubehelix iterates from 0 to steps-1, computes cubehelix.rgb(i/steps, opts), normalizes each RGB component by dividing by 255, pushes results into an array, and returns it.
createCubehelix(steps, opts) builds and returns an array of length steps by looping i from 0 to steps-1, mapping cubehelix.rgb(i/steps, opts) values to v/255.
Creates and returns an array of length steps where each element is cubehelix.rgb(i/steps, opts) normalized by dividing each RGB component by 255.
Converts an array of color channel arrays into a flattened image-data array by scaling each channel value by 255, appending alpha 255, and concatenating all pixels.
`toImageData` maps each color array by multiplying components by 255, appending alpha 255, then reduces by concatenation to return one flattened image-data array.
`toImageData` converts an array of color arrays by multiplying each channel by 255, appending alpha 255 to each color, and returning one flattened concatenated array.
Converts an array of color arrays into a flattened RGBA array by scaling each component by 255, appending alpha 255, and concatenating all pixels.
Creates a compressed color array by sampling the input at evenly spaced indices based on factor, iterating with computed step size, and returns the collected sampled colors.
`compress(colors, factor)` computes a sampling step from `colors.length/factor`, iterates while `i < colors.length`, pushes `colors[i|0]` into `data`, and returns the sampled array.
Compress takes a colors array and factor, computes len and step from lengths, iterates i<colors.length in step increments, pushes colors[i|0], and returns data.
Iterates through the colors array in increments of step, pushes colors[i|0] into a new array each iteration, and returns the resulting array.
Converts an array of RGB-like value arrays into colormap stops, assigning each stop a rounded 0–1 index based on position and 0–255 rounded RGB values.
`toColormap(data)` iterates through `data`, creating stops with index percentages rounded from `i*100/(data.length-1)` and RGB values rounded from each element scaled by 255, then returns `stops`.
toColormap iterates through data, building stops with index as rounded percentage position over data.length−1 and rgb as each value scaled to 0–255, then returns stops.
Converts an array of RGB-like value arrays into a colormap array of objects with normalized rounded index and 0–255 rounded rgb values, returning the new array.
Creates a URI from src, initializes a BackgroundDownloader, creates a download to storageFile, and returns the asynchronous start operation from download.startAsync().
startDownload creates a Windows Foundation.Uri from src, builds a BackgroundTransfer.BackgroundDownloader download to storageFile, and returns download.startAsync() to begin the transfer.
Creates a Windows URI from src, instantiates a BackgroundDownloader, creates a download to storageFile, and returns the download.startAsync() operation.
Starts a background download from the source URI to the specified storage file by creating a downloader and download operation, then returns download.startAsync().
Removes `app[key]`, logs and rewrites the error message to indicate `app.key` unexpectedly errored using `err.message`, then rethrows the same error.
Deletes `app[key]`, builds and logs an `"app.${key}" unexpectedly errored` message using `err.message`, overwrites `err.message` with it, and rethrows the same error.
`errorHandler(app, key, err)` deletes `app[key]`, builds and logs an `"app.${key}" unexpectedly errored` message using `err.message`, overwrites `err.message`, then rethrows `err`.
Logs a debug message when `app[key]` unexpectedly errors, deletes `app[key]`, and then rethrows the original `err` without catching it.
Deletes `app.connection`, logs and rewrites the error message to include the unexpected connection error details, then rethrows the same error.
errorHandler deletes app.connection, builds and logs an error message using err.message, replaces err.message with that message, and then rethrows the same error.
`errorHandler(app, err)` deletes `app.connection`, builds and logs a message using `err.message`, replaces `err.message` with that message, and rethrows the same error.
Handles an unexpected app.connection error by logging a debug message with err.message and err, deleting app.connection, and then rethrowing the original error.

Creates an Application instance (self-instantiating if needed), applies env/default options, wraps Schema input, initializes properties, and either sets ClusterManager for master clustering or requires queueName otherwise.

Initializes an Application instance, returning a new one if not called with `new`, normalizing/defaulting options/env values, configuring clustering checks, requiring queueName for consumers, and setting core properties.

Initializes an Application instance (self-instantiating if not called with `new`), normalizes/defaults options, validates `queueName` based on clustering/master status, sets instance fields, and returns the instance.

Initializes an Application instance (self-instantiating if needed), applies environment/default options, sets up EventEmitter and ClusterManager, warns/asserts queueName based on clustering, and defines a queueNames getter.
Trims and validates a shard string prefix and `v1` version, requires a numeric parameter, then returns a Prefix/Suffix/NextToLast instance by name or throws errors.
Trims a shard string, validates nonempty input, required PREFIX, version 'v1', and parameter presence, then returns a Prefix/Suffix/NextToLast instance with parsed integer param or throws Error.
`parseShardFun` trims a shard string, validates non-empty/PREFIX/`v1`/parameter presence, parses the numeric parameter, and returns `new Prefix|Suffix|NextToLast(param)` or throws errors.

Parses a trimmed shard path string, validating non-empty input, required prefix, version `v1`, and parameter presence, then returns Prefix/Suffix/NextToLast(parsed integer) or throws errors for invalid cases.
Returns true if both nodes are ignored, have matching checksums, or pass the native `a.isEqualNode(b)` comparison; otherwise returns false.
`isEqualNode(a, b)` returns true if both nodes are ignored, their checksums are equal, or `a.isEqualNode(b)` is true; otherwise it returns false.
isEqualNode returns true if both nodes are ignored, their checksums are equal, or a.isEqualNode(b) is true; otherwise it returns false.
Returns true if both nodes are ignored, their checksums match, or `a.isEqualNode(b)` is true; otherwise returns false.
Recursively dispatches a non-bubbling, non-cancelable event of the given type on a node and its descendants when each node has a key, then returns the original node.
Dispatches a non-bubbling, non-cancelable Event of the given type on nodes where getKey(node) is truthy, recurses through all children, and returns the original node.
Dispatches a non-bubbling, non-cancelable Event of the given type on node when getKey(node) is truthy, recursively processes children, and returns the original node.
Recursively dispatches a non-bubbling, non-cancelable Event of the given type on a node and its children while iterating children, then returns the original node.

Initializes socket logging, validates multiaddr when strict mode is enabled, optionally performs nonce-based crypto challenge/verification with pub key, then finalizes join or returns error/nonce via callback.

Handles a socket join by validating multiaddr and optional crypto-challenge flow, tracking metrics, issuing/verifying nonces and signatures, then returning errors, a nonce challenge, or finalizing join via callback.

Handles a socket join by validating multiaddr, optionally enforcing crypto-challenge nonce/signature checks, incrementing join metrics, and returning cb errors, a nonce challenge, or joinFinalize’s result.

Handles a socket join by validating multiaddr and required pub key, issuing/verifying a crypto nonce challenge, incrementing join metrics on failures, and returning errors, nonce, or finalized join via callback.
Returns null for falsy input, '' when anyOf/allOf/oneOf exists, 'object' if type is missing, recursively appends [] for arrays, otherwise returns value.type.
Returns null for falsy input, '' if anyOf/allOf/oneOf exists, 'object' when type is missing, recursively resolves array item type plus '[]', otherwise returns value.type.
Returns null for falsy value, '' if anyOf/allOf/oneOf exists, 'object' without value.type, dataType(value.items||{})+'[]' for array type, otherwise value.type.
Returns null for falsy input, '' for schemas with anyOf/allOf/oneOf, 'object' when type is missing, recursively formats array item types with [], otherwise returns value.type.
Retrieves and returns the value associated with an Event from `privateData`, asserting that the retrieved value is not null and reporting the event if the assertion fails.
`pd(event)` gets `privateData.get(event)`, asserts the result is not null (logging an Event-object expectation message with `event`), and returns that retrieved value.
Retrieves private data for the given event via privateData.get(event), asserts the result is not null (logging an Event-object expectation message), and returns that result.
Retrieves and returns private data for the given event via `privateData.get(event)`, asserting the result is non-null and reporting the event if the assertion fails.
Creates a configurable, enumerable property descriptor whose getter returns `pd(this).event[key]` and setter assigns `value` to `pd(this).event[key]`.
defineRedirectDescriptor(key) returns a configurable, enumerable property descriptor whose getter and setter read and write pd(this).event[key], respectively.
defineRedirectDescriptor(key) returns a configurable, enumerable descriptor whose getter returns pd(this).event[key] and whose setter assigns value to pd(this).event[key].
Creates and returns a configurable, enumerable property descriptor whose getter and setter read and write `pd(this).event[key]`, with no additional conditions or error handling.

Creates and returns a CustomEvent subclass wrapper around BaseEvent, but returns BaseEvent unchanged when proto has no keys, adding only non-inherited proto properties as method or redirect accessors.
Creates and returns a CustomEvent subclass of BaseEvent, but returns BaseEvent unchanged when proto has no keys, adding only proto properties absent from BaseEvent.prototype via descriptors.
Creates and returns a CustomEvent subclass of BaseEvent, returning BaseEvent unchanged when proto has no keys, and only defining wrapped prototype properties not already on BaseEvent.prototype.
Creates and returns a CustomEvent subclass of BaseEvent with proto’s keys defined as call or redirect descriptors based on descriptor.value type, or returns BaseEvent when proto has no keys.
Returns `Event` when `proto` is null or `Object.prototype`; otherwise retrieves a cached wrapper for `proto` or recursively defines, caches, and returns one based on its prototype chain.
`getWrapper(proto)` returns `Event` when `proto` is null or `Object.prototype`; otherwise it gets or recursively defines, caches, and returns a wrapper for `proto`.
`getWrapper(proto)` returns `Event` when `proto` is null or `Object.prototype`; otherwise it gets a cached wrapper or recursively defines, caches, and returns one for `proto`.
Returns Event for null or Object.prototype; otherwise gets a cached wrapper for proto or defines one from its prototype chain, caches it, and returns it.
Creates and returns a new wrapper instance for an event by selecting a Wrapper based on the event’s prototype and passing eventTarget and event to it.
`wrapEvent` gets a wrapper class for `event`’s prototype via `getWrapper(Object.getPrototypeOf(event))` and returns a new `Wrapper` instance initialized with `eventTarget` and `event`.
Creates a wrapper class from the event’s prototype via getWrapper(Object.getPrototypeOf(event)) and returns a new Wrapper instance initialized with eventTarget and event.
Returns the result of invoking the wrapper obtained from getWrapper(Object.getPrototypeOf(event)) with eventTarget and event, with no additional conditions or error handling.
Retrieves and returns the listener collection for an event target from `listenersMap`, throwing a `TypeError` if no entry exists (i.e., the target is null/invalid).
Gets listeners for an eventTarget from listenersMap, throws a TypeError if the retrieved listeners value is null, and otherwise returns the listeners.
`getListeners` retrieves `listenersMap.get(eventTarget)`, throws a `TypeError` if the result is `null`, and otherwise returns the retrieved `listeners`.
Returns the listeners associated with eventTarget from listenersMap, throwing a TypeError if listeners is null because this is not an EventTarget object.
