Creates and returns a drill accessor for nested object keys, defaulting root/path, recursively drilling via own-property checks, and exposing val/exists plus set, conditional update, and bound invoke methods.
Returns `drill`; if `object` is a function, it binds `object` to `_context` using `Function.prototype.bind.call` before returning.
Filters and sorts tasks (respecting verbose hidden-task filtering), builds a usage/tasks help text with aligned task names and multiline comments, and returns the lines joined by newlines.
printTasks filters hidden tasks based on verbose, sorts them, formats each task name with aligned comment lines, and returns a newline-joined usage/tasks help text string.
Filters hidden tasks using `verbose`, sorts them, builds aligned task/comment lines (including additional comment lines), and returns a newline-joined usage/tasks help string.
Filters and sorts tasks by visibility, formats each task name with aligned comment lines, and returns the joined usage header string “Usage: gulp [task] [task2] ...\n\nTasks: ”.
Formats text into a padded column by defaulting left/right offsets to 3 when undefined, then returning left spaces, the text, nonnegative width-based trailing spaces, and right spaces.
formatColumn returns text padded with spaces, defaulting undefined offsetLeft/offsetRight to 3, and adding left/right offsets plus nonnegative width-based trailing padding.
Formats a column by defaulting undefined left/right offsets to 3, then returns left spaces + text + max(width−text.length,0) spaces + right spaces.
Returns the text padded with offsetLeft leading spaces, enough trailing spaces to reach at least width (or none if text is longer), and offsetRight trailing spaces.
Creates and returns a new TaskDoc instance that initializes a TaskList and invokes gulp.Gulp on itself, with TaskDoc’s prototype set to gulp.
Defines `inheritGulp`, which creates `TaskDoc`, initializes `this.taskList` with `new TaskList()`, calls `gulp.Gulp.call(this)`, sets `TaskDoc.prototype = gulp`, and returns `new TaskDoc()`.
Defines `inheritGulp`, which creates a `TaskDoc` constructor that initializes `this.taskList`, calls `gulp.Gulp.call(this)`, sets `TaskDoc.prototype = gulp`, and returns `new TaskDoc()`.
Creates and returns a new TaskDoc instance by calling TaskDoc(), with no inputs, conditions, asynchronous behavior, or error handling.
Checks whether a truthy item is a Promise by testing util.types.isPromise, constructor name 'Promise', or a non-objectInstance with a function then property, returning true or false.
Checks whether `item` is promise-like: returns false if falsy, otherwise true if `util.types.isPromise(item)`, constructor name is `'Promise'`, or `item.then` exists and is a function.
Checks whether `item` is promise-like: returns false if falsy, otherwise true if `util.types.isPromise(item)`, constructor name is `'Promise'`, or `item.then` exists and is a function.
Determines whether an input is a Promise, returning false for falsy values and otherwise true if util.types.isPromise, constructor name "Promise", or a then-function check succeeds.
hasCallback converts a function to string, rejects async or no-argument arrow/unknown forms, extracts declared parameters from standard or arrow syntax, and returns whether any parameter exists.
Determines whether a function declares any parameters by parsing its string form, rejecting async and empty-parameter arrow functions, and returning true if the extracted argument list is non-empty.
Determines whether a function declares any parameters by parsing its string form, rejecting async and no-argument arrow functions, and returns true if extracted arguments are nonempty.
Converts `fn` to a string, rejects async or empty-parameter arrow forms and missing arrow matches, extracts parameters, trims whitespace, and returns whether any argument text exists.

deferAdd increments parentChain waiting counters/IDs, queues a deferred task with id/prerequisites, runs task with prerequisite context values, stores result by id, updates completion, and triggers execution callbacks.

Adds a deferred task by incrementing parentChain.waitingOn, initializing/pushing waitingOnIds, queuing id/prereq/payload in self._deferred, and returns nothing while triggering execution as dependencies complete.
Increments `parentChain.waitingOn`, initializes and appends `id` to `waitingOnIds`, queues a deferred task with defaulted `id/prereq`, runs it with prerequisite context values, and returns nothing.
Adds a deferred task by recording its id, prerequisites, and payload, updates waiting dependencies, executes task with prerequisite context values, stores result by id, and triggers execution flow.
Finds the first incomplete task; if index check fails logs unknown-task timeout and structure, otherwise logs timed-out task details, then always fires and returns the timeout event trigger.
Finds the first incomplete task in `this._struct`, logs either unknown-task or timed-out task details depending on index validity, then triggers and returns `this.fire('timeout')`.
Finds the first incomplete task index in `this._struct`, logs either unknown-task or task-specific timeout details based on index validity, then fires and returns `this.fire('timeout')`.
Finds the first incomplete task index, logs timeout diagnostics (including unknown task, full structure, and task/type with elapsed timeout), then fires a 'timeout' event.

Runs a function or promise with optional context/args, normalizes run(fn,finish,args), detects promise/callback/sync forms, catches errors, and always calls finish(err,result) with mapped promise outcomes.
Runs a function with optional context/args, normalizing when context is a function, handling promise/callback/sync paths, and invoking finish with error or result (defaulting promise errors).
Runs `fn` with `context` and optional `args`, normalizing when `context` is a function, handling promise/callback/sync paths, and invoking `finish` with error or result (no return value).
Runs `fn` with `context`, handling promise, callback-style, or synchronous execution; it checks `isPromise`/`hasCallback`, forwards results or errors to `finish`, and returns nothing.
Runs `iter` asynchronously up to a finite `limit` (default 10), stopping when an error or falsy result occurs, then calls `callback` with error state and returns `this`.
runWhile starts up to a finite limit (default 10) of asynchronous iter calls, repeatedly schedules more until an error or falsy result, invokes callback on completion/error, and returns this.
Runs `iter` concurrently up to finite `limit` (default 10), repeatedly scheduling until error or falsy result, then calls `callback(err[,res])` when done, and returns `this`.
Runs a loop from 0 to limit, checks Number.isFinite(limit), schedules invoke with setTimeout each iteration, and returns this.
Resets internal structure and pointer, rebuilds `_context` with current state and bound `hook`/`fire` methods, and reassigns `_options.context` only if it previously referenced the old context.
Resets internal structure and pointer, checks whether `_options.context` equals previous `_context`, rebuilds `_context` with bound methods and state references, and returns nothing.

Resets internal structure and pointer, rebuilds `_context` with current state and bound methods, checks whether `_options.context == _context`, and returns by optionally reattaching `_options.context` to `_context`.
`reset` takes no arguments and invokes `bind(this)` on both `this.hook` and `this.fire`, with no explicit conditions, asynchronous behavior, errors, or return value.
Returns null if comment or tags are missing; otherwise scans this.comment.tags for a tag with matching name and returns its value, or null if none matches.
Returns the value of the first tag in this.comment.tags whose name strictly equals the given name, or null if comment/tags are missing or no match is found.
Returns the value of the first this.comment.tags entry whose name strictly equals the given name, or null if comment/tags are missing or no match is found.
Returns the value of the first comment tag whose name matches the input, but returns null if comment/tags are missing or no matching tag is found.
Checks a file against blacklist and whitelist regexes, returning false if blacklisted, true if whitelisted, false if whitelist exists but doesn’t match, otherwise true.
checkPattern returns false if blackList is a RegExp matching file; otherwise, if whiteList is a RegExp it returns true only when it matches file, else true.
Checks a file against blacklist and whitelist regexes: returns false if blacklist is a RegExp matching file, else for whitelist RegExp returns its match result, otherwise true.
Checks a file against blacklist/whitelist patterns: returns false if blacklist is a matching RegExp, true if whitelist matches, false if whitelist is RegExp without match, otherwise true.

Initializes a seven-segment digit object with configurable height/width, angle, ratios, and digit defaults, choosing fixed height unless only width is provided, then positions and returns the instance.

Initializes a seven-segment object from optional settings, defaulting angle/ratios/digit when undefined, choosing fixed height unless width is provided, then creates segment structures and positions them.

Initializes a seven-segment display object from optional settings, applying defaults for angle/ratios/digit, checking defined height and width to set fixed-dimension mode, then positions segments and returns nothing.
Calls `Segment()` seven times, then invokes `this._positionSegments()` on the current receiver, with no explicit conditions, asynchronous behavior, error handling, or return value.
Handles a change event by returning early if remove() is true; otherwise resolves with an array of input.files, and rejects with any caught error.
`onChange(event)` tries to remove something and returns early if that call is truthy; otherwise it resolves with `Array.from(input.files)`, and rejects with `error` if an exception occurs.
`onChange(event)` tries to remove something and returns early if successful, otherwise resolves with `Array.from(input.files)`, and on any thrown error rejects with that error.
Handles a change event by removing a listener, resolving with an array of selected input files unless remove() returns undefined, and rejecting with any caught error.
Initializes or reuses a RemoveObserverPrivate instance for node by checking Self.get(node), creating and storing one if missing, then associates ref with that same instance.
Initializes a RemoveObserverPrivate for node only if Self.get(node) is falsy, stores it in Self, then maps ref to that self via Self.set, returning nothing.
Initializes or retrieves a RemoveObserverPrivate for node via Self.get, creates and stores one if absent, then stores that self under ref using Self.set.
Initializes a remove-observer instance by retrieving existing state for node, creating private observer data from node, and storing it in Self for both node and ref.

Parses an expression by repeatedly appending results from `nextChain(expr)` until it returns `false`, temporarily resetting and then restoring `currentIndex` and `propertyRegex.lastIndex`, and returns the concatenated string.

parsePropertyChains(expr) resets currentIndex and propertyRegex.lastIndex to 0, repeatedly appends nextChain(expr) results until false, restores previous index states, and returns the concatenated parsedExpr string.
parsePropertyChains resets indices, repeatedly calls nextChain(expr) until it returns false, concatenates each returned chain into parsedExpr, restores previous indices, and returns parsedExpr.
Parses property chains from `expr` by repeatedly calling `nextChain(expr)` until it returns `false`, then returns `parsedExpr`.
Parses a function-call expression into a guarded call string, adjusting scope by index, checking callee type and optional chained-property access, and returning the transformed link expression.
Parses a function-call expression into a guarded link string, handling index 0 versus others and dot-property access checks, then returns the transformed link.

parseFunction builds and returns a guarded function-call access string, adjusting link by index, adding null-safe reference wrapping when expr at propertyRegex.lastIndex is '.', and parsing call arguments.
Parses a function call from expr, normalizes link with this/global context, replaces the ~~insideParens~~ placeholder using parsed property chains from call arguments, and returns the updated link.

Parses a bracketed function-call segment, checks whether the next character at `propertyRegex.lastIndex` is `.`, and returns the reconstructed link with parsed inner property chains and reference handling.
Parses bracket notation in an expression by extracting and parsing the bracket contents, checking whether the next character is a dot, and returning the reconstructed link string.

parseBrackets extracts a function-call’s bracket contents, parses link/index parts, checks whether expr at propertyRegex.lastIndex is '.', prefixes references accordingly, replaces the placeholder with parsed chains, and returns link.
Parses a function-call expression by extracting bracket contents, evaluating link parts, replacing `~~insideBrackets~~` with parsed property chains, and returning the updated link string.
If referenceCount is truthy, prepends expr with a var declaration for _ref1 through _refN (N = referenceCount), then returns the resulting expr string.
`addReferences` checks whether `referenceCount` is truthy, prepends `expr` with `var _ref1..._refN;\n` built via a 1-to-`referenceCount` loop, and returns `expr`.
`addReferences(expr)` checks `referenceCount`; if truthy, it builds `_ref1`…`_refN`, prepends `var <joined refs>;\n` to `expr`, and returns the resulting `expr` string.
Builds a comma-separated list of reference names from `_ref1` to `_ref{referenceCount}` by looping from 1 to `referenceCount`, then returns `expr`.
Checks whether `t` is truthy; if not, creates an `AssertionError` with message `m`, optionally captures its stack trace, and throws the error.
`assert(t, m)` checks whether `t` is truthy; if not, it creates and throws `new AssertionError(m)`, optionally capturing stack trace via `Error.captureStackTrace(err, assert)`.
assert(t, m) throws a new AssertionError(m) when t is falsy, optionally capturing its stack trace via Error.captureStackTrace(err, assert), and otherwise returns normally.
Throws an AssertionError with message m and captured stack trace when t is falsy; otherwise, it returns nothing.
Builds and returns openers/closers arrays, adding {}, [], (), or reversed )/( pairs when options.braceException, bracketException, parenException, or empty are truthy.
Builds `openers` and `closers` arrays by checking `options.braceException`, `bracketException`, `parenException`, and `empty`, pushing corresponding symbol pairs, then returns `{ openers, closers }`.

getExceptions builds openers and closers arrays, adding paired symbols when options.braceException, bracketException, parenException, or empty are truthy, then returns an object containing both arrays.
Creates and returns an object containing `openers` and `closers` arrays populated with bracket and parenthesis characters, including an extra `)` and `(` entry.
Returns false if tokens already have space; otherwise, with ALWAYS true returns false for closing parenthesis or opener exceptions, else true, and with ALWAYS false returns opener-exception status.
Determines opener spacing by returning false if left and right already have space, otherwise under ALWAYS returns false for closing parens or non-exceptions, else returns opener-exception status.

`shouldOpenerHaveSpace(left, right)` returns false if tokens already have space, or when ALWAYS and right is a closing parenthesis; otherwise returns exception-based spacing (`!isOpenerException(right)` or `isOpenerException(right)`).
Returns false if there is already space between left and right or right is a closing parenthesis; otherwise returns whether right is not an opener exception.
Returns whether a closer should have space by rejecting opening-parenthesis left tokens or existing spaces, then returning the inverse or direct closer-exception check based on ALWAYS.

Determines closer-token spacing by returning false if left is an opening parenthesis or tokens already have space, otherwise returning !isCloserException(left) when ALWAYS, else isCloserException(left).

Determines whether a closer should have space by returning false for opening-paren left tokens or existing token spaces, otherwise returning !isCloserException(left) when ALWAYS, else isCloserException(left).
Returns false if left is an opening parenthesis or already spaced from right; otherwise returns true unless left is a closer exception, in which case false.
Returns false if right is a Line token, tokens are on different lines, or no space exists; otherwise returns opener-exception status based on ALWAYS (direct or negated).
Returns false if right is a Line token, not on the same line as left, or lacks intervening space; otherwise returns opener-exception status based on ALWAYS.
shouldOpenerRejectSpace returns false if right is a Line token, tokens are on different lines, or no space exists; otherwise it returns isOpenerException(right) when ALWAYS, else its negation.
Returns false if right is a Line token, tokens are on different lines, or no space exists between them; otherwise returns isOpenerException(right).
Returns false if left is an opening parenthesis, tokens are on different lines, or no space exists; otherwise returns isCloserException(left) when ALWAYS, else its negation.

Checks whether closer spacing should be rejected: returns false unless left is an opening parenthesis, left/right share a line, and have a space; then returns isCloserException(left) if ALWAYS, otherwise its negation.
Determines whether a closer should reject space by requiring left be an opening parenthesis, left/right on the same line with space between, then returning exception status based on ALWAYS.
Returns whether a closer should reject space by requiring left to be an opening parenthesis, on the same line as right, with space between them, and not a closer exception.
Defines a non-enumerable, writable, configurable property named `key` with value `val` on `obj` using `Object.defineProperty`.
Defines `obj[key]` via `Object.defineProperty` with `value` set to `val`, `configurable` and `writable` true, and `enumerable` false, returning no explicit value.
Defines `obj[key]` via `Object.defineProperty` with `configurable:true`, `enumerable:false`, `writable:true`, and `value:val`, returning whatever `Object.defineProperty` returns.
Defines a non-enumerable, writable, configurable property named key on obj with value val using Object.defineProperty, and returns nothing.
Converts an argument to a number, returning 0 for NaN, returning 0 or ±Infinity unchanged, otherwise returning its sign multiplied by the floored absolute value.
Converts the argument to a number, returns 0 if NaN, returns it unchanged if 0 or ±Infinity, otherwise returns sign(number) × floor(abs(number)).
ToInteger converts argument to a number, returns 0 if NaN, returns number if 0 or ±Infinity, otherwise returns sign(number) multiplied by floor(abs(number)).
Converts argument to a number, returning 0 for NaN, the original numeric value for 0 or ±Infinity, otherwise the signed integer truncated toward zero.
Converts the argument to an integer length and returns 0 if it is nonpositive; otherwise returns the smaller of that integer and 2^53−1.
Converts the argument to an integer length, returning 0 if the result is nonpositive; otherwise returns the smaller of that length and 2^53−1.
Converts argument to an integer length, returns 0 if the result is nonpositive, otherwise returns the smaller of that length and 2^53−1.
Converts argument to an integer length and returns 0 if it is nonpositive; otherwise returns the lesser of that length and 2^53−1.
Converts the input to an object, creates an ArrayIteratorPrototype-based iterator, initializes iterated object, next index 0, and iteration kind internals, then returns the iterator.
Creates an array iterator by converting `array` to an object, creating an object from `ArrayIteratorPrototype`, setting internal iterated-object, next-index (0), and kind slots, then returning it.
Creates an array iterator by converting `array` to an object, creating an `ArrayIteratorPrototype`-based object, setting internal iterated object, next index `0`, and kind, then returning it.
Converts the input to an object, creates an ArrayIteratorPrototype-based iterator, initializes its iterated object, next index (0), and iteration kind internals, then returns the iterator.

Returns a resolver function that throws if its bound [[Promise]] is not an object, returns undefined if already settled, otherwise stores resolution, marks fulfilled, clears reactions, and triggers resolve reactions.

PromiseResolve returns function F(resolution) that throws TypeError if F.[[Promise]] isn’t an object, returns undefined unless status is unresolved, otherwise stores resolution, updates internals, and triggers resolve reactions.

PromiseResolve returns function F(resolution) that throws TypeError unless F.[[Promise]] is an object, returns undefined unless unresolved, otherwise resolves internals and returns TriggerPromiseReactions(reactions, resolution).
Returns a resolver function that validates its bound promise is an object and unresolved, then stores the resolution, clears reactions, marks resolved, and triggers resolve reactions.
Creates an executor function that throws a TypeError if capability [[Resolve]] or [[Reject]] is already defined; otherwise it stores the provided resolve and reject in them.

GetCapabilitiesExecutor returns function F(resolve, reject) that throws TypeError if promiseCapability.[[Resolve]] or [[Reject]] is not undefined, otherwise stores resolve and reject in those internal slots.
GetCapabilitiesExecutor returns a function that retrieves F['[[Capability]]'], throws TypeError unless its [[Resolve]] and [[Reject]] are undefined, then stores resolve and reject internally.
Returns an executor function that throws TypeError if capability [[Resolve]] or [[Reject]] is already defined, otherwise stores the provided resolve and reject into those internal slots.
Returns a handler that rejects with a TypeError if resolving to itself, otherwise creates a new capability, assimilates thenables, and returns chained handling or direct fulfillment-handler result.

Creates and returns handler F(x) that rejects on self-resolution, returns caught errors from capability/thenable updates, chains thenables via promiseCapability promise.then, otherwise fulfills with x.

Returns a function that rejects on self-resolution, otherwise creates a promise capability, updates from thenable, returning errors if thrown, chaining handlers if thenable, else calling fulfillmentHandler with x.

Returns a function that rejects self-resolution, creates a new promise capability, assimilates thenables via UpdatePromiseFromPotentialThenable, chains handlers when thenable, otherwise calls fulfillmentHandler with x.
Reports a lint error at the token start when a space appears before the token, and returns a fixer that removes the range between the previous and current tokens.
Reports a lint error at token.loc.start when a space exists before token.value, and returns a fixer removing the range between tokenBefore.range[1] and token.range[0].
Reports a lint error at token.loc.start for a space before token.value and returns a fixer removing text from tokenBefore.range[1] to token.range[0].
Reports a lint error when called, indicating no space should precede the token, and provides an autofix that removes characters between the previous token’s end and current token’s start.
Reports a lint error at the token’s start location requiring a following space after the token value, and returns a fixer that inserts one space after it.
Reports a lint error at token.loc.start for the given node, stating a space is required after token.value, and returns a fixer inserting one space after token.
Reports a lint error for a node at token.loc.start requiring a space after token.value, and returns a fixer that inserts one space after the token.
Reports a lint error when spacing after a token is missing, indicating a space is required after the token value and providing an autofix to insert one space.
Reports a lint error at the token’s start location requiring a preceding space before the token value, and returns a fixer that inserts one space before it.
Reports a lint error on `node` at `token.loc.start` requiring a space before `token.value`, and returns a fixer that inserts one space before `token`.
Reports a lint error on `node` at `token.loc.start` requiring a space before `token.value`, and returns an autofix that inserts one space before `token`.
Reports a lint error at the token’s start location requiring a space before the token value, and provides an autofix that inserts a space before that token.

Computes random latitude and longitude offsets from input coordinates using distance, latitude-degree scaling, cosine(latitude), and random signs, then returns the adjusted `{lat, lon}` destination coordinates.

generateDestinationLonLat takes {lat, lon}, computes latitude and longitude offsets from getDistance()/LAT_DEGREE and getSign(), with longitude additionally divided by Math.cos(lat), and returns updated coordinates.
Generates destination coordinates by adding signed distance-based latitude and longitude offsets (longitude scaled by LAT_DEGREE·Math.cos(lat)) to input lat/lon, returning `{ lat, lon }`.
Generates destination coordinates by computing latitude and longitude offsets using two distance values, random signs, and cosine of latitude, then returns updated `{lat, lon}`.
Executes `git log --pretty="%an <%ae>"`, throws an error if execution fails or stderr exists, and otherwise calls `cb` with null error and reversed author lines array.
`gitAuthors` runs `git log --pretty="%an <%ae>"`, throws an `Error` if `er` or `stderr` is truthy, otherwise calls `cb(null, stdout.split('\n').reverse())` and returns the `exec` call.
`gitAuthors` runs `git log --pretty="%an <%ae>"`; if `er` or `stderr` exists it throws `Error(er || stderr)`, otherwise it returns `cb(null, stdout.split('\n').reverse())`.
Runs `git log --pretty="%an <%ae>"`, throws an error if `er` or `stderr` exists, otherwise calls `cb(null, reversedAuthorLines)` and returns the `exec` invocation.
Looks up a GitHub user login by searching email first then full name, optionally adds OAuth authorization, tracks API messages, and returns callback(err, p) with p.login if found.
Looks up a GitHub login for p by email then fullname, optionally prints progress and adds OAuth header, sets p.login on first match, and returns via callback(err,p).
lookupGithubLogin optionally adds OAuth authorization, prints a dot if requested, searches GitHub users by email then fullname, sets p.login on first match, and returns via callback(err,p).
`lookupGithubLogin` trims `process.env.OAUTH_TOKEN`, writes a dot to stdout, and requests GitHub’s user search API for `p.email`; it performs no condition checks and returns nothing.
Validates that the message starts with keyczar_util.VERSION_BYTE, throws an error with the first character code if not, then returns extracted keyhash and remaining message segments.
_unp​ackOutput verifies message.charAt(0) equals keyczar_util.VERSION_BYTE, throws an Error with the first byte code if not, then returns {keyhash, message} sliced from the input.
Unpacks an output message by verifying its first character equals `keyczar_util.VERSION_BYTE`, throwing an error otherwise, then returning `{keyhash, message}` split using `KEYHASH_LENGTH`.
Validates the first character equals keyczar_util.VERSION_BYTE, throws an error with its char code if not, then returns an object containing extracted keyhash and remaining message substrings.
Computes a SHA-1-based RSA key hash by hashing the trimmed big-number modulus and exponent (with length-prefixing via `_hashBigNumber`) and returns `KEYHASH_LENGTH` bytes of the digest.
Creates a SHA-1 digest, hashes the RSA public key’s n and e big-number components into it, and returns digest bytes truncated to keyczar_util.KEYHASH_LENGTH.
Computes a SHA-1 hash over the RSA public key’s `n` and `e` big numbers, then returns the digest bytes truncated to `keyczar_util.KEYHASH_LENGTH`.
Computes an RSA key hash by SHA-1 hashing the public key’s modulus and exponent, then returns the first keyczar_util.KEYHASH_LENGTH bytes of the digest.

Creates an RSA key wrapper with keyhash and modulus size, providing OAEP encryption and signature verification that unpacks/checks signature keyhash, hashes the message, and returns packed ciphertext or verify result.
Creates an RSA key wrapper with keyhash and modulus bit size, adding encrypt and verify methods that unpack/check signature keyhash, then returns packed ciphertext or verification boolean.
Creates an RSA key wrapper with keyhash and size, whose encrypt returns packed RSA-OAEP ciphertext, verify unpacks/checks signature keyhash then verifies digest, and returns the wrapper object.
Creates and returns a key by hashing the provided rsaKey and evaluating rsaKey.n.bitLength(), with no explicit conditions, asynchronous behavior, or error handling.
Initializes an EachSubject proxy by creating and storing a subject for each element, naming each with optional index plus parent description, and copying the parent failure message.

EachSubject initializes ProxyBase, creates elementSubjects by wrapping each element with subjectFactory.newSubject, names each using elementName plus optional index and subject description, copies failureMessage, and returns nothing.
Initializes `elementSubjects`, then for each element creates a new subject, names it with optional index plus parent description, copies `failureMessage`, and pushes it into `this.elementSubjects`.
Initializes each element in `elements` as a new subject via `subjectFactory`, names it using `elementName`, optional index, and `subject.describe()`, and stores each in `this.elementSubjects`.
Creates a DeferredSubject wrapper for a promise that, on resolve, replays recorded calls on a new value-based subject, on reject records a failure message, and returns a thenable/catchable promise.

Initializes an eventual subject from a subject and promise, running a derived subject on promise fulfillment, failing the subject with a formatted message on rejection, and returning the original value/reason.

Initializes a DeferredSubject wrapper for a subject and promise, running assertions on resolved values, failing the subject on rejection, and returning the original resolved value or rejection reason.
Initializes a deferred subject tied to a promise, creating and running a value-based subject on fulfillment, failing the original subject on rejection, and exposing bound then/catch methods.
Initializes a PromiseSubject by invoking Subject with failureStrategy and value, then makes it thenable by binding and exposing the underlying value’s then and catch methods.
Initializes `PromiseSubject` by calling `Subject` with `failureStrategy` and `value`, then assigns `this.then` and `this.catch` to `this.value`’s bound promise methods, returning nothing.
PromiseSubject calls Subject with failureStrategy and value, then assigns this.then and this.catch to this.value.then/catch bound to this.value, returning nothing explicitly.
Initializes a PromiseSubject by invoking Subject with failureStrategy and value, then binds the promise’s then and catch methods to this.value for consistent context.
Retrieves a value by resolved key from store data, optionally resolves references when referenceDepth>0, uses cache when store isn’t writable, and returns cached or computed value.
Resolves the key, reads `referenceDepth` (default 1), returns cached value when store is non-writable and cache exists, otherwise gets data, optionally resolves references, caches, and returns it.

Resolves the key, optionally uses `_getCache` when store isn’t writable, gets `property.get(store._data,key)`, resolves references if `referenceDepth>0`, caches result when applicable, and returns the value.
Returns a cached value for key and referenceDepth if available; otherwise resolves the key, gets it from store._data, resolves references, and returns the resulting value.
Recursively resolves reference-valued elements in arrays and plain objects from store data up to the given depth, returning transformed copies or the original value when depth is exhausted.
Recursively resolves reference values in arrays and plain objects using store helpers, stops when decremented depth is below zero, and returns the transformed or original value.
Recursively resolves reference values in arrays and plain objects using store helpers, stops when decremented depth is below zero, and returns the transformed or original value.

Recursively resolves reference-like items in arrays or plain-object properties using store data while depth remains nonnegative, and returns the original value unchanged when depth is exhausted or non-iterable.
Escapes ASCII control characters in a string (using named escapes or octal codes), optionally clips it with ellipsis when `opts.clip` is exceeded, and returns the result wrapped in double quotes.

formatString escapes ASCII control characters in value (named escapes for \n,\r,\t,\b,\v,\f; otherwise octal), optionally clips to opts.clip with "...", and returns the result wrapped in double quotes.
Formats a string by escaping ASCII control characters (named escapes or octal), optionally clipping to opts.clip with ellipsis when exceeded, and returns the result wrapped in double quotes.
Escapes control characters in value using named or octal sequences, optionally computes a clipped slice length from options.clip, and returns the escaped result wrapped in double quotes.

Reads and parses a JSON config file, optionally merges it over an extended config when `config.extends` exists, removes `extends`, and returns the resulting config or `{}` on errors.
Reads and parses a JSON config file, and if it has an extends path, parses that file, merges current config into it, removes extends, and returns the resulting config object.
getConfig reads and parses a JSON file into config, optionally loads and merges an extended config when config.extends exists, removes extends, and returns config, swallowing errors.
Reads and parses a config file, optionally parses and merges an extended config after deleting its extends field, ignores any caught errors, and returns the config object.
Checks whether a file matches any ignore pattern using case-insensitive, basename-aware minimatch rules, returning true on the first match and false if none match.
`isIgnored(file)` returns whether any `ignorePatterns` entry matches `file` using `minimatch`, checking patterns case-insensitively and against basename via `nocase: true` and `matchBase: true`.
`isIgnored(file)` returns whether any `ignorePatterns` entry matches `file` using `minimatch`, checking patterns with `nocase: true` and `matchBase: true`.
Returns whether `file` matches any `ignorePatterns` entry by checking each pattern with `minimatch` using case-insensitive and basename matching options.
extractStyles normalizes line endings, keeps only lines inside `<style`…`</style` blocks while blanking others, then returns the joined text with `{$...}` placeholders replaced by `{}`.

extractStyles removes carriage returns, keeps only lines between “<style” and “</style” markers (blanking others), then returns them joined by newlines with {$path.like.this} placeholders replaced by “{}”.

extractStyles normalizes line endings, scans lines for `<style`/`</style` to toggle block capture, stores only in-block lines (blank otherwise), then returns joined text with `{$...}` placeholders replaced by `{}`.

extractStyles normalizes carriage returns, processes each line to keep content only within `<style`/`</style` blocks, blanks others, then returns the joined text with `{$...}` placeholders replaced by `{}`.
Reads a source file from argv[3], optionally transforms its contents via a pre-commit modifier using argv[2] as filename, ignores modifier errors, and returns a resolved Bluebird promise object.
Reads filename and UTF-8 source from process arguments, optionally transforms source via a required pre-commit modifier in a try/catch, then returns Bluebird.resolve({ filename, src }).
Reads filename from process.argv[2] and UTF-8 source from argv[3], optionally transforms source via a required pre-commit modifier in try/catch, then returns Bluebird.resolve({filename, src}).
Reads UTF-8 content from the file at process.argv[3], applies the pre-commit modifier plugin to it, and returns a Bluebird-resolved object containing filename and src.
Loads `.js` plugin modules from `.git-hooks/pre-commit-plugins/plugins` under the current working directory, skipping non-JS files and read errors, and returns a checker-name-to-module object.

Loads `.js` plugin files from `.git-hooks/pre-commit-plugins/plugins` under `process.cwd()`, skipping non-JS files, requiring each module into `checkers` by basename, and returning the `checkers` object.
loadFileCheckerPlugins reads the plugins directory, requires each `.js` file into `checkers` keyed by filename without extension, ignores errors, and returns the `checkers` object.
Reads `.git-hooks/pre-commit-plugins/plugins`, loads only `.js` files as checker modules keyed by filename without extension, ignores errors silently, and returns an empty object.
Increments a global counter, writes the indicator to stdout, and when counter equals filesLength or is divisible by lineLength, prints spacing plus formatted “counter / filesLength” and a newline.
Increments `counter`, writes `indicator`, and when `counter === filesLength` or `counter % lineLength === 0`, writes spacing, a padded `counter / filesLength` line, and a newline; returns nothing.
`printCounter` increments `counter`, writes `indicator`, and when `counter === filesLength` or `counter % lineLength === 0`, writes spacing, formatted `counter / filesLength`, and a newline.
`printCounter(indicator)` writes the indicator, computed line spacing, formatted counter/filesLength values, and a newline to stdout, returning nothing and performing no conditional checks.
Converts input to a string and percent-encodes reserved, control, and non-ASCII characters using uppercase UTF-8 byte sequences (1–4 bytes), returning the joined encoded string.

Encodes a string by percent-escaping reserved, control, and non-ASCII characters, converting matched characters to uppercase UTF-8 byte sequences based on code-point range, and returns the joined result string.

Encodes a string by percent-escaping reserved/non-ASCII/newline characters, converting matched char codes into 1–4 UTF-8-style `%HH` sequences based on code-point range, and returns the joined result.
Encodes a string by replacing characters matching reserved, control, or non-ASCII patterns with percent-encoded UTF-8 bytes based on code point size, then returns the joined result.
Decodes percent-encoded hexadecimal byte sequences (`%XX`, case-insensitive) in a string by converting each match to its character code and returns the resulting string.
Decodes a string by replacing every case-insensitive `%` followed by two hexadecimal digits with its corresponding character, returning the transformed string.
`decode` replaces every case-insensitive `%` followed by two hex digits in `string` with the corresponding character code and returns the transformed string.
Decodes all percent-encoded hexadecimal byte sequences (%XX, case-insensitive) in the input string by converting each to its character code and returns the resulting string.
Generates a random nonce string (default 64-bit length) by selecting hex byte values from 0x20–0x7E, looping over full 4-byte groups and any remaining bytes, then returning it.
Generates a nonce string by defaulting key_length to 64 when falsy, computing byte-based iteration/remainder counts, and returning concatenated random entries from a fixed hex-like character array.
Generates a random nonce string of hexadecimal-like byte values, defaulting key_length to 64 when falsy, then appending 4 values per full group plus remainder, and returns it.
Generates and returns a nonce value by calling rand() repeatedly across loops iterating up to key_iter and key_remainder based on the provided key_length.
Builds a sorted header string from non-object, non-empty, defined params as encoded key="value" pairs, optionally prepends an encoded realm entry, and returns the comma-separated result.
Builds a header string by encoding and including non-object, non-empty, defined params as `key="value"`, sorting them, optionally prepending encoded `realm`, and returning them joined by `, `.
Builds a sorted header string from params by encoding and including only non-object, non-empty, defined values, optionally prepending encoded realm, then returns entries joined by ", ".
Builds an authorization header string by encoding each `params` key/value pair, sorting them, prepending an encoded `realm` entry, and returning the comma-separated result.

Builds a signature base string by encoding non-empty header and query parameters, sorting them lexicographically by key then value, joining as key=value pairs, and returning method&encodedURL&encodedParameters.

Builds a signature base string by encoding non-undefined, non-empty header and query parameters, lexicographically sorting key/value pairs, then returning method, encoded URL, and encoded joined parameters separated by “&”.

Builds an OAuth-style signature base string by encoding non-empty, defined header/query parameters, lexicographically sorting key/value pairs, then returning method, encoded URL, and encoded joined parameters concatenated with “&”.
Builds a signature base string by encoding and collecting header and query parameters, lexically sorting by key then value, and returning `method&encodedUrl&encodedJoinedParams`.

Adds translation objects to `I18n.translations`, recursing through locale-keyed maps when `locale` is undefined, ignoring non-objects, and otherwise initializing or merging the specified locale’s translations.
Adds translations into `I18n.translations`, returning early unless `translations` is an object; if `locale` is undefined it recursively adds each key, otherwise initializes or merges locale entries.

Adds translation objects into I18n.translations, returning early if translations isn’t an object, recursively processing all locales when locale is undefined, and otherwise setting or merging locale translations.
Adds translations for a locale by recursively processing each key, returning undefined if translations isn’t an object or locale is undefined, then merging into I18n.translations[locale].
Initializes an RPC EventEmitter, asserting valid RPC instance and Contact inputs (and optional replyto Contact), sets hooks, pending calls, contact/logger, readyState to 0, then opens it.

Initializes an RPC instance by asserting valid RPC/contact inputs (and optional replyto Contact), setting hooks, pending calls, contact/logger/readyState, invoking EventEmitter and open(), and returning nothing.
Initializes an RPC instance by asserting valid RPC/contact (and optional replyto Contact), invoking EventEmitter, setting hooks/state/contact/logger defaults, and calling open(), returning nothing.
Initializes an RPC instance by asserting valid instance, contact, and options.replyto Contact arguments, invoking EventEmitter initialization, and opening the RPC connection on this.
Initializes a Channel event emitter with an id and exchange, listens for exchange events matching that id, re-emits received messages as 'message', and sets unlimited listeners.
Channel(id, exchange) initializes an EventEmitter-based channel, stores id and exchange, subscribes exchange.on(id) to re-emit incoming messages as 'message', and sets unlimited listeners.
Channel initializes an EventEmitter-based instance, assigns id and exchange, listens on exchange for this id, re-emits received messages as 'message', and sets max listeners to 0.
Initializes a Channel by invoking EventEmitter, subscribing to exchange messages on this.id to re-emit them as 'message' events, and setting unlimited listeners with setMaxListeners(0).
Validates that `func` is a function, optionally binds it to `context` when truthy, appends it to `steps`, and returns `continuable` for chaining.
Validates `func` is a function, optionally binds it to `context` if provided, pushes it onto `steps`, and returns `continuable` for chaining.
Validates `func` is a function, optionally binds it to `context` when provided, pushes the resulting function onto `steps`, and returns `continuable` for chaining.
Validates `func` is callable, binds it to `context`, pushes it onto `steps`, and returns `continuable`.
Returns undefined for falsy input or the exact “ERROR: No README data found!” string; otherwise extracts and returns the first non-heading, non-empty text block as a trimmed single line.
Extracts a description from input text by returning undefined for falsy or specific error strings, then trimming/splitting lines, skipping heading/empty starts, and returning trimmed joined content.

extractDescription returns undefined if d is falsy or equals "ERROR: No README data found!", otherwise trims/splits lines, skips leading headers/blank lines, collects following nonblank lines, and returns trimmed text.
Returns undefined for missing input or the exact “ERROR: No README data found!” string; otherwise returns the first non-header, non-empty trimmed README paragraph joined into one line.
Adds a comment object after asserting numeric start, skips duplicates when lastCommentStart is at or beyond start, optionally adds range/loc, and returns undefined after pushing to comment lists.
Adds a comment if start is numeric and newer than state.lastCommentStart, updates lastCommentStart, optionally sets range/loc, pushes to extra.comments, and returns early otherwise undefined.
Creates a comment object, asserts start is numeric, skips if start is not after state.lastCommentStart, optionally adds range/loc, pushes to extra.comments, and maybe leading/trailing arrays.
Adds a comment object when start is valid and not before the last comment start, asserting numeric position and pushing it to comments, leadingComments, and trailingComments arrays.
Consumes the next token and throws an unexpected-token error unless its value matches the given keyword and its type is Identifier when contextual is true, otherwise Keyword.
Lexes the next token, verifies its type matches Identifier when contextual is true or Keyword otherwise and its value equals keyword, and returns throwUnexpected(token) on mismatch.
Parses the next token with `lex`, and if its type (Identifier when contextual, otherwise Keyword) or value differs from `keyword`, calls `throwUnexpected(token)`; otherwise returns normally.
Parses the next token with `lex()`, then calls `throwUnexpected(token)`, unconditionally signaling an unexpected token error without returning a value.

Parses a bracketed array initializer, handling elements, elisions, spread, and optional comprehension `for`/`if`, enforcing comprehension/spread validity, and returns a comprehension or standard array expression node.

Parses an array initializer, handling elements, holes, spread, and optional `for`/`if` comprehension clauses, enforcing comprehension/spread validity, and returns either a comprehension or standard array expression AST node.

Parses an array initializer, handling elements, elisions, spread, and optional comprehension `for`/`if` clauses with syntax/error checks, returning either a comprehension expression or array expression.

Parses an array initializer, handling elements, spread, and optional comprehension (`for`/`if`) syntax, throwing comprehension or spread-placement errors, and returns a comprehension or array expression node.

Parses a property function body with option-based async/generator and parameter defaults, checks strict-mode restricted first parameter names when named, restores parser state, and returns a marked function expression.

Parses a property function body with option-provided or default params/defaults, temporarily sets strict/yield/await flags, checks strict restricted-name violations, restores prior state, and returns a marked function expression.

Parses a property function by setting/restoring strict and yield/await parser state, defaulting params/defaults, checking strict restricted names, and returning a marked delegated function expression AST node.
Parses a property function by creating a marker and concise body, checks if the first parameter name is restricted to throw a tolerant strict-name error, and returns the marked function expression.

Parses a left-hand-side expression, and if followed by `++` or `--` without a line terminator, validates strict-mode and assignment legality, then returns a postfix expression or the original expression.

Parses a left-hand-side expression, returns it unless lookahead is a punctuator postfix ++/-- without line terminator, then validates strict/restricted and assignable LHS, builds and returns postfix expression.

Parses a left-hand-side expression, returns it unchanged unless lookahead is a punctuator postfix ++/-- without line terminator, then validates strict/LHS rules, consumes token, and returns postfix expression.
Parses a postfix expression by returning the left-hand expression unless next token is ++/--, then validates line terminator, restricted word, and LHS rules, and returns postfix expression.
Parses unary expressions by handling prefix ++/--, +/−/~ /!, and delete/void/typeof recursively, enforcing strict-mode and left-hand-side checks, and otherwise returns a postfix expression.

Parses unary expressions by checking token/keyword types and operators (++/--, +/-, ~, !, delete/void/typeof), enforcing strict-mode and left-hand-side errors, and returning unary or postfix expression nodes.
Parses unary expressions by checking token/keyword types and operators (++/--, +/-, ~, !, delete/void/typeof), enforcing strict-mode LHS/delete rules, and returning unary or postfix expression nodes.

parseUnaryExpression returns parsePostfixExpression unless a unary/prefix operator matches, then recursively parses and returns a marker-applied unary expression, validating ++/-- left-hand side and strict-word/delete constraints.

Recursively converts assignment expressions into binding patterns, validating object/array/spread/identifier forms, enforcing spread-last and init-only properties, rejecting restricted words and invalid LHS forms, and mutating/returning the expression.

Reinterprets an expression as an assignment binding pattern, recursively converting object/array/spread forms, validating property kinds and restricted identifiers, throwing specific errors on invalid cases, and returning nothing.

Reinterprets an expression as an assignment binding pattern by converting object/array expressions, recursively processing members/elements/spreads, validating property kinds and restricted identifiers, throwing syntax errors, and returning nothing.

Reinterprets an expression as an assignment binding pattern by recursively processing object/array members and arguments, throwing errors for invalid assignment targets, restricted identifiers, spread-order violations, or object-pattern spreads.
Parses an expression statement by creating a marker, parsing an expression, consuming a semicolon, and returning the marker applied to a created expression-statement node.
Parses an expression statement by creating a marker, parsing an expression, consuming a semicolon, and returning markerApply(marker, delegate.createExpressionStatement(expr)).
parseExpressionStatement creates a marker, parses an expression, consumes a semicolon, and returns markerApply(marker, delegate.createExpressionStatement(expr)).
Parses an expression statement by creating a marker, parsing an expression, consuming a semicolon, and returning the marker-applied expression statement node from the delegate.

Parses a return statement, tolerantly errors outside function bodies, handles space-plus-identifier and line-terminator cases, optionally parses an expression unless before `;`, `}`, or EOF, and returns a marked ReturnStatement node.

Parses a `return` statement, errors tolerantly if outside a function body, conditionally parses an argument based on spacing/line-terminator/token checks, consumes semicolon, and returns a marked ReturnStatement node.

Parses a return statement, errors tolerantly outside function bodies, conditionally parses an argument based on whitespace/line-terminator and token checks, consumes semicolons, and returns a marked ReturnStatement node.
Parses a return statement: after `return`, it returns null if a line terminator follows, parses an expression unless next char starts an identifier, then consumes semicolon and returns node.
Creates and returns a new object by copying own enumerable properties from `object`, then overriding or adding own properties from `properties` when `hasOwnProperty` is true.
Creates and returns a new object by copying own enumerable properties from object, then own enumerable properties from properties, with later properties overriding earlier ones.
Creates and returns a new object by copying own enumerable properties from object, then overriding/adding own enumerable properties from properties, checking hasOwnProperty in both for-in loops.
Creates and returns a new result object by copying own enumerable properties from object and properties, checking hasOwnProperty for each entry during both loops.
Reflows text to a maximum line width by splitting on hard-break patterns (GFM-aware), wrapping words when adding one would exceed width, and returning newline-joined sections.
Reflows text to a maximum width by splitting sections with GFM/non-GFM hard-return regexes, wrapping words when column plus word length exceeds width, and returning newline-joined sections.
Reflows text to a target width by splitting sections via GFM/non-GFM hard-return regex, wrapping words when column+word length exceeds width, and returning newline-joined reflowed sections.
Splits text into sections and words, wraps words to new lines when adding one would exceed width, preserves spacing between words, and returns sections joined by newline characters.
Validates `fp` is a string, throws a `TypeError` otherwise, returns true for POSIX absolute paths on non-Windows, and otherwise returns the Windows absolute-path check result.
Checks that `fp` is a string (else throws `TypeError`), returns `true` if not Windows and `isAbsolute.posix(fp)` is true, otherwise returns `isAbsolute.win32(fp)`.
Checks whether `fp` is a string, throws `TypeError` otherwise, returns true for non-Windows POSIX-absolute paths, and otherwise returns `isAbsolute.win32(fp)`.
Checks that `fp` is a string (throwing a `TypeError` otherwise), returns `true` for POSIX absolute paths on non-Windows, and otherwise returns the Windows absolute-path check result.
Repeats a string `num` times, throwing a TypeError if input isn’t a string, handling `num` 1 or 2 directly, and returning the built repeated string truncated to exact length.
Repeats a string num times, throwing TypeError if str isn’t a string, returning early for num 1 or 2, and otherwise returning a cached, doubled-build substring of length str.length*num.
Repeats a string num times, throwing TypeError if str isn’t a string, returning early for num 1 or 2, and otherwise returning a cached, doubled-build substring result.
Repeats a string num times, throwing a TypeError if str is not a string, handling num 1 or 2 directly, then looping and returning a length-limited substring.
Returns a new array containing only the first occurrence of each element from `arr`, filtering out duplicates by checking membership in a `Set` and adding unseen values.
`uniqSet` filters an array by tracking seen elements in a `Set`, adding and keeping only elements not already present, and returns the deduplicated array.
`uniqSet(arr)` filters `arr` using a `Set`, adding each element only if `seen.has(el)` is false, and returns an array containing first occurrences of unique elements.
Returns a filtered array of unique elements from `arr` by tracking seen values in a `Set`, adding and keeping each element only if it hasn’t appeared before.
Appends the current command and message to state.error, logs it when nonempty, exits if config.fatal is true, and throws an empty string unless _continue is truthy.
Handles errors by initializing `state.error` if null, appending `state.currentCmd + ': ' + msg + '\n'`, logging when `msg.length>0`, exiting if `config.fatal`, and throwing `''` unless `_continue`.
Initializes state.error if null, appends “currentCmd: msg\n”, logs when msg.length>0, exits with code 1 if config.fatal, and throws '' when !_continue.
Logs `state.error` and exits the process with code 1; if `_continue` is falsy, it first throws an empty string, and it returns nothing.
Checks whether a path exists and is a directory, then tests write permission by creating and deleting a temporary file, returning the directory path or false.
Checks whether `dir` exists and is a directory, then tests writability by creating and deleting a random file, returning `dir` if writable, otherwise `false`.
Checks whether `dir` exists and is a directory, then verifies writability by creating and deleting a random test file, returning `dir` if successful, otherwise `false`.
Returns false if dir is missing, nonexistent, not a directory, or any write-test error occurs; otherwise writes and deletes a random test file and returns dir.
Recursively creates a directory by checking whether its parent exists; if it does, creates the directory immediately, otherwise creates parent directories first, then the target directory.
Recursively creates a directory by checking whether its parent exists, creating the target immediately if it does, otherwise creating the parent first, then the target, and returns undefined.

`mkdirSyncRecursive(dir)` computes `baseDir = path.dirname(dir)`, creates `dir` immediately if `baseDir` exists, otherwise recursively creates `baseDir` first, then creates `dir`, returning early only in the first case.
Recursively creates a directory by first ensuring its parent exists; if the parent already exists it returns undefined, otherwise it creates parent directories then the target with mode 0777.
Returns an empty array if `p` is falsy; otherwise splits `p` into an array using `;` on Windows (`common.platform === 'win'`) or `:` on other platforms.
splitPath returns an empty array when p is falsy; otherwise, it returns p split by ';' if common.platform is 'win', or by ':' for other platforms.
splitPath returns an empty array when p is falsy; otherwise, it splits p by ';' if common.platform is 'win', or by ':' for other platforms.
splitPath returns an empty array if p is falsy; otherwise it splits p by ';' on Windows (common.platform === 'win') or by ':' on non-Windows platforms.
Updates process stdout by reading a stdout file, returning early if silent, missing, or unchanged in length, otherwise writing only newly appended content and caching it.
updateStdout exits if options.silent is true, stdoutFile is missing, or file content isn’t longer than previousStdoutContent; otherwise writes only new stdout text and updates previousStdoutContent.

updateStdout exits if silent or stdoutFile is missing, otherwise reads stdoutFile, returns if content didn’t grow, writes only newly appended text to process.stdout, and updates previousStdoutContent.
updateStdout returns undefined if silent mode is on or the stdout file is missing, or if no new content exists; otherwise it writes the unread stdout substring.
Initializes a GNTP object with type, host and port defaults, builds a GNTP/1.0 request string, initializes resources and attempt counters, and returns the constructed instance.
Initializes a GNTP object by defaulting opts to {}, setting type, host (opts.host or localhost), port (opts.port or 23053), request string, resources array, and attempt counters.
Initializes a GNTP instance by defaulting opts to {}, setting type, host (opts.host or localhost), port (opts.port or 23053), request string, resources, attempts, and maxAttempts.
Defines `GNTP` with parameters `type` and `opts`, performs no checks or calls, and has no specified asynchronous behavior, errors, or return value.
The Growly constructor initializes a Growly object with default properties: appname set to "Growly", count to 0, registered false, and notifications, labels, host, and port undefined.
Initializes a Growly instance by setting default properties (appname, notifications, labels, count, registered, host, port) without condition checks, and returns no explicit value.
Creates a Growly object by initializing appname to 'Growly', count to 0, registered to false, and notifications, labels, host, and port to undefined, returning nothing.
Growly is a function with no inputs, conditions, calls, asynchronous behavior, error handling, or specified return value.
Initializes a Command instance with empty commands, options, execs, and args arrays, disables unknown options, and stores the provided name in _name.
The Command constructor initializes commands, options, _execs, and _args as empty arrays, sets _allowUnknownOption to false, assigns _name from the name argument, and returns the instance.
Creates a Command object by initializing commands, options, _execs, and _args as empty arrays, setting _allowUnknownOption to false, and assigning _name from the name parameter.
Defines a `Command` function that takes `name` as input, performs no checks or calls, handles no async or errors, and has no specified return value.
Returns a new array of elements from `array` not found in `values`, returning `[]` for empty input and using cache/index lookups, with special handling for common non-NaN comparisons.
Returns a new array of elements from `array` not found in `values`, immediately returning empty for falsy/empty `array`, using cache-based lookup for large `values`, and excluding strict matches.

Returns elements from `array` not in `values`, immediately returning `[]` for empty arrays, using cache-based lookup for large `values`, and excluding strict-equal matches (including self-equality checks).
Returns a new array of elements from `array` not found in `values`, returning empty when `array` is empty, using cache/index checks and pushing unmatched values to `result`.
Returns the lookahead token at offset p (default 0), filling missing lookahead entries via lex.token(), and returns state.tokens.next if no token exists and next is "(end)".
Returns the p-th lookahead token (default 0), filling missing lookahead entries via lex.token(), and if no token exists while next token id is "(end)", returns state.tokens.next.
Returns the token at lookahead index p (default 0), filling missing lookahead entries via lex.token(), and returns state.tokens.next when no token exists and next.id is "(end)".
Iterates while j <= i, returning state.tokens.next if no token exists and the next token is "(end)"; otherwise it lexes tokens and finally returns t.

Parses and returns an identifier via `optionalidentifier`; if absent, handles `...` rest syntax with ESNext and validity checks, otherwise reports `E030`, conditionally advances, and may return nothing.

Parses an identifier-like token, returning optionalidentifier/identifier results when valid; handles spread/rest “...” with esnext and punctuator checks, warns/errors on invalid tokens, and may return undefined.

Returns an existing optional identifier if found; otherwise handles spread/rest “...” syntax checks and warnings, returning parsed identifier, undefined on invalid spread target, or advancing after non-semicolon errors.

Parses an identifier, returning an existing parsed value or undefined if next token isn’t an identifier, while handling/advancing spread (`...`) tokens and issuing related warnings/errors recursively.
Determines whether input is a non-JSON block or JSON value, warns on destructuring assignment outside ESNext, parses statements for blocks, and otherwise enables JSON mode and parses a JSON value.

Determines context via `lookupBlockType`; if not JSON, optionally warns when destructuring assignment appears outside ESNext and parses statements, otherwise enables JSON mode/laxbreak, parses a JSON value, and returns nothing.

Determines parsing mode via `lookupBlockType`; if `block.notJson`, optionally warns when not ESNext and destructuring assignment, then calls `statements`, otherwise enables JSON/laxbreak mode and calls `jsonValue`.
Determines the current block type, warns about destructuring assignment when not in ESNext mode, then processes either statements or a JSON value depending on context.
Creates and returns an Assertion for `this`, unwrapping primitive wrapper objects (`String`, `Number`, `Boolean`) via `valueOf()` when `this` is an instance of those types.
Returns a new Assertion for `this.valueOf()` when `this` is a String, Number, or Boolean wrapper object; otherwise returns a new Assertion for `this` itself.
`shouldGetter` returns a new `Assertion`, using `this.valueOf()` when `this` is a `String`, `Number`, or `Boolean` instance, otherwise using `this`, with `null` and `shouldGetter` passed through.
Returns an Assertion for the current value, using this.valueOf() when this is a String, Number, or Boolean object, otherwise using this, with shouldGetter as context.
Checks whether an object matches a type by returning `instanceof` for function values, `Array.isArray` for `'array'`, otherwise comparing `typeof object` to the given value.
Checks an object against a type descriptor by returning `object instanceof value` when `value` is a function, `Array.isArray(object)` when `value` is `'array'`, otherwise `typeof object === value`.
Checks whether object matches value by returning object instanceof value when value is a function, Array.isArray(object) when value is 'array', otherwise typeof object === value.
Checks whether `object` matches `value` by returning `object instanceof value` if `value` is a function, `Array.isArray(object)` if `value` is `'array'`, otherwise `typeof object === value`.
Determines how many arguments a key should consume via aliases, sets an error if fewer than required remain, assigns those arguments to the key, and returns the new index.
Consumes the number of arguments required for key (via aliases), sets an error if remaining args after index i are insufficient, assigns consumed args with setArg, and returns i+toEat.
eatNargs computes required argument count for key, sets an error if remaining args after i are fewer than needed, assigns that many following args via setArg, and returns i+toEat.
Consumes the next `toEat` arguments after index `i` for `key`, setting each via `setArg`, and returns `i + toEat`, erroring if insufficient arguments follow.

setConfig applies defaults/aliases, loads each specified config file path from argv or lookup, sets args from file unless CLI explicitly set them, and records an error for invalid user-specified config files.
Initializes config lookup defaults, then for each configured key loads a resolved config file path and sets argv values only when undefined or defaulted, assigning an error on load failure.

setConfig initializes config aliases/defaults, iterates config keys, loads each resolved config file when a path exists, applies config values to argv under override/default conditions, and sets error on load failure.
Initializes argv defaults/aliases, then for each configured config key loads a resolved config file path and applies its properties only when argv lacks the key or it was defaulted.
Iterates over each key in `obj` (or `{}`), builds alias arrays from `opts.alias`, adds camelCase variants for dashed names, and returns nothing while populating `aliases`/`newAliases`.

extendAliases iterates Object.keys(obj||{}), builds aliases[key] from opts.alias[key] or [], adds camelCase versions for hyphenated entries, maps each alias to [key,...otherAliases], and returns nothing.

Computes the maximum first-column string length from an array or object-converted table, optionally capping it to half of `wrap` when `wrap` is truthy, and returns that width.
Computes the maximum length of each row’s first element in table (converting non-arrays via Object.keys mapping), optionally caps it when wrap is truthy, and returns width.

normalizeAliases gets demanded and options from yargs, iterates option aliases, and for each alias applies description, demand message, and boolean/count/string/normalize/array settings to its key.
normalizeAliases iterates option aliases, propagating each alias’s description, demanded message, and type flags (boolean, count, string, normalize, array) to its primary key via yargs methods.

Finds and returns the element after the first odd-indexed form whose value equals attrName in attrForms when attrForms is an array; otherwise returns undefined.
Checks if `attrForms` is an array, finds an odd-indexed element whose `value` equals `attrName` while recording its index, and returns `attrVal`.
Writes the given string synchronously to the specified file path, then logs a cyan “create : ” message with that path to the console.
`write(path, str)` synchronously writes `str` to the file at `path` using `fs.writeFileSync`, then logs a cyan “create : ” prefix plus the path to console.

Writes the given string synchronously to the specified path using fs.writeFileSync, then logs a cyan “create : ” message with the path, and returns nothing.
Creates a directory at the given path with mode 0755 only if it doesn’t already exist, and logs a “create” message unless `silent` is true.
Creates a directory at path with mode 0755 only if it doesn’t already exist, and if not silent logs a “create : ” message; otherwise returns nothing.

Creates a directory at the given path if it doesn’t already exist, using mode 0755, and logs a cyan “create :” message with the path.
Checks a directory path synchronously; returns false if it contains files, aborts on caught errors with a code, and otherwise returns true when empty or unreadable without code.

Checks whether a directory is empty by reading its entries; returns false if any exist, aborts on caught errors, and otherwise returns true.
Creates a request object that builds Basic Authorization from grel.token if present, otherwise grel.user and grel.password, then sets headers, stores grel, and initializes content to null.

Initializes a GrelRequest by building authString from grel.token or grel.user/password, setting Basic Authorization, Accept, and User-Agent headers, storing grel, and returning with content set to null.
Initializes a GrelRequest by choosing token-based or user/password authString, setting Basic Authorization, Accept, and User-Agent headers, storing grel on this, and setting this.content to null.
Creates a Base64-encoded string from `authString` using `new Buffer(authString).toString('base64')`, takes `grel` as input, and has no explicit conditions or return value.
Parses response data as JSON (or `{}`), checks if status code is 200–206, and calls the callback with an error for “Bad credentials” or non-2xx, otherwise success data.
Parses `data` as JSON (or `{}`), checks whether `res.statusCode` is 200–206, and calls `callback` with an error for `"Bad credentials"` or with parsed JSON otherwise.

Splits text by OS-independent newlines, returns {} unless the first line is '---', otherwise returns an object with header and remaining content separated at the next '---'.
Splits text into lines, returns {} if the first line isn’t '---', otherwise finds the next '---' before the last line and returns {header, content} sections.
Splits content into lines, returns {} unless the first line is '---', then finds the next '---' and returns {header, content} slices joined by newlines.
Splits text by lines, returns {} unless the first line is '---', then captures lines through the next '---' as header and returns remaining lines as content.
Adds actions by calling `add` with a string, recursively processing each element of an array, or iterating object keys to call `add(type, value)`; otherwise returns nothing.
addActions processes actions by adding a string directly, recursively handling arrays, and iterating object keys to add key-value pairs, returning undefined.
addActions processes actions by calling add(actions) for strings, recursively forEach(addActions) for arrays, and add(type, actions[type]) for each key when actions is an object.
Processes an actions input by adding it directly, recursively handling arrays, or iterating object keys to add each type-action pair based on its runtime type.

Creates a Metalsmith plugin that defaults `options.key` to `'untemplatized'`, strips leading newlines from each file’s contents, stores the result as a Buffer on that key, and calls `done` asynchronously.

Initializes options with default key `'untemplatized'`, then returns a plugin function that iterates files, strips leading newlines from each file’s contents, stores it as a Buffer under that key, and calls done asynchronously.

Returns an array of `data` values by taking `Object.keys(data)`, slicing from index 0 to `this.headers.length`, and mapping each key to `data[key]`.

Returns an array of values from `data` for keys up to `this.headers.length`, by taking `Object.keys(data)`, slicing to that length, and mapping each key to `data[key]`.
Creates a job from trigger/function/data, stores it by id, enqueues its id and execution time, sets a timer only if queue is empty or earlier than current head, and returns the job id.
Creates a job from trigger/function/data, stores it by id, queues its id/time, and if no current job or earlier execution time, resets timer; always returns job.id.
Creates a job from trigger/function/data, stores it by id, enqueues `{id,time}`, and if no current job or earlier execution time, resets timer; always returns `job.id`.
Creates a job from trigger, function, and data, computes its execution time, compares it with the current queued job, queues it, optionally sets a timer, and returns job.id.

Defines and registers a type validator, deriving validator/name from a function type, rejecting non-function validators, primitive overrides, or conflicting existing validators, and returns the validator.

Defines a type validator by normalizing function types, requiring validator to be a function, rejecting primitive overrides and conflicting registry validators, storing it in registry, and returning validator.

Parses the type name, throws if it matches a primitive type, removes its registry entry, and returns the removed type’s validator or false if none existed.

Parses the type, lowercases its name as a registry key, throws if it is primitive, deletes its registry entry, and returns the removed validator or false.
Parses the type, lowercases its name, throws a TypeException if it is a primitive, deletes it from the registry otherwise, and returns the validator or false.

Parses the type, resolves a validator from primitives or registry, throws a TypeException for unknown types, validates indexed types via arrayValidation, otherwise returns validator(value, previous, attributeName).

Parses the type, resolves a validator from primitives or registry, throws TypeException if none exists, runs arrayValidation when indexes are present, otherwise returns validator(value, previous, attributeName).
Parses the type, resolves a validator from primitives or registry, throws TypeException if none exists, then returns arrayValidation for indexed types or validator(value, previous, attributeName).
Parses the type definition, verifies a primitive or registered validator exists (else throws `TypeException`), validates indexed types via `arrayValidation`, and returns the validator’s result.
Returns an array combining all keys from `primitives` with each `registry` entry’s `type` value by mapping over `registry` keys and concatenating the results.
Returns an array combining Object.keys(primitives) with, for each key in registry, the value of registry[type].type mapped from Object.keys(registry).
Returns an array combining primitive object keys with each registry key’s corresponding `registry[type].type` value by concatenating `Object.keys(primitives)` and a mapped `Object.keys(registry)`.

Loads a module from a string path, returning merged `_SETTINGS` with the module object only if loading succeeds and yields a plain object; otherwise returns nothing.
Loads a module from src only when src is a nonempty string and require succeeds with a plain object, returning merged _SETTINGS and file; otherwise returns undefined.
